#2015. Celtic boss addresses midfielder’s ‘deja vu’ return and gives update on duo who were posted missing

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hopes Luke McCowan’s performance in the 4-1 win over St Mirren can be a catalyst to reignite his Parkhead career.

O’Neill watched his side open up a seven-point gap on second-placed Rangers, who face Motherwell on Saturday evening, blowing away St Mirren before half-time thanks to goals from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (33), Camilo Duran (40) and McCowan (42). Callum McGregor (63) added a fourth, with Killian Phillips (69) scoring a consolation penalty for the away side.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Dealt a double blow ahead of the game, midfield pair Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur both ruled out after picking up injuries on international duty, O’Neill handed McCowan his first start in over two months in the centre of the park alongside Oxlade-Chamberlain.

McCowan has suffered in the last few months, dropping out of the matchday squad after a high-profile error in the defeat to LASK during the Champions League playoffs. Forced to delete his Instagram account to escape personal abuse from sections of the online support, the former Dundee captain had played just 14 minutes since being hauled off at half-time in a 1-0 home defeat to Rangers on September 20.

“I thought he did really well for us,” was O’Neill’s assessment of McCowan’s return to the starting line-up. “It was his first full game for a considerable amount of time. He got the ball once and he played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought ‘oh gosh, here we go’. But he roared back. Took the goal great, and I’m really pleased for him because he’s a really genuine lad.

“It has been tough [for him]. I thought in the game against Rangers, he was thrown into position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I thought it felt like deja vu for him after his last game against Rangers at the back end of last season, too. For him today, I felt that was a big boost for him. I’m pleased that there’s a bit of competition for places [in midfield] now. Which is good. But I am pleased that him and Alex got on the field and were able to play. That itself is a confidence booster.”

Duran had the ball in the net for Celtic after five minutes but assistant referee signalled for an offside. The home side thought they’d taken the lead again just after the quarter hour mark, with Duran the disappointed party once more. Blasting home the rebound after Jota’s shot was parried away by Jacob Chapman, the frustrated Colombian looked to sky as the flag went up for offside in the build up for a second time.

A misplaced pass from McCowan signalled a groan from the home crowd as Celtic frustration crept in, however, they needn’t have worried, finding their opener via Oxlade-Chamberlain just after the half-hour mark, with the experienced midfielder slamming home from close range after a positive forward run and cross from Hyun-Jun Yang on the right-wing.

It was no less than the home side deserved, but the momentary VAR check for the opener followed by a blocked goal-bound effort from Killian Phillips offered some unexpected anxiety in the immediate aftermath. O’Neill’s side added further unnecessary stress on a bitterly cold Glasgow afternoon when Yang somehow failed to square to Duran when clean through on goal.

The striker finally got on the scoresheet with a fine side-footed finish from a Kieran Tierney cross shortly before the break.

A moment of redemption followed just 120 seconds later when the returning McCowan collected a neat cut back from Jota in the area to fire home first time beyond Chapman, effectively killing the game before the break.

His first goal since the 5-1 win over Kilmarnock on August 9, a relatively muted celebration followed from McCowan as he was congratulated by his teammates. Virtually out of the picture at Celtic in recent weeks, he’ll hope it’s not his last and that his unexpected reprieve can lead to an extended spell in his boyhood club’s engine room. The victory already wrapped up in nine first-half minutes, McGregor’s placed shot added to the scoreline just after the hour mark, with Phillips’ penalty after a foul from goalkeeper Sam Johnstone on Calvin Ramsay in the box just a consolation.

O’Neill also addressed the omission of Haissem Hassan during his press-match conference and the fitness of Baur and Alistair Johnston. Quashing rumours that the Egyptian was left out against Kilmarnock prior to the international break because he was “unpopular” within the squad earlier this week, the 74-year-old has insisted that both Hassan and Kasper Hogh, who was an unused substitute, will have a part to play against Torreense in the Europa League on Thursday night.

“Kasper will be ready for Thursday,” said O’Neill. “That’s the point. We’re going to need him on Thursday. For want of a better word, it’s more rotation than anything else. Kasper is fine. He’ll [Haissem] will be there for Thursday as well. He’s missed a couple of games. He didn’t come back until Friday from the international break, a couple of them didn’t.

“We were worried about Duran after he travelled halfway around the world, but he was amazing in training.

“Baur is in a boot. If that injury stretches to end of January, we’ll think about making a change [to the Europa League squad]. Alistair was getting a scan and some treatment this weekend in Dublin. We’ll find out about that and get an update. I’m hoping it’s going to be good news. He’s feeling decent within himself now.”

#2014. Hull City v Brighton and Hove Albion: Unity between contrasting groups key to Tigers' success

Last season, Hull won promotion via the Championship play-offs on the back of a squad who has been the course and distance in the division.

That group was put together under restrictions which stopped Hull buying or even paying a loan fee for players in 2025-26. With the restrictions lifted and a ticket for the gravy train that is the world's most lucrative domestic football league, they have broadened their horizons.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Eighteen players were signed – although Joe Gelhardt was a loan made permanent – and are overwhelmingly young and new to English football.

Yet according to 22-year-old Cho – who spent his childhood flitting between England and France – as well as performing brilliantly in the season’s first ten games, the old guard have welcomed the next generation.

It is why Hull go into Sunday's Premier League game at home to Brighton and Hove Albion still unbeaten on the banks of the Humber this season. Whoever pulled on the black and amber, the Tigers simply would not be able to compete if their squad was fractured.

"The lads that were here before, they've been amazing with the new lads," says the French-born player in an English accent which shows why he has represented both countries in international age-group football.

"I don't think there's two groups. Everyone's joking with everyone, everyone's working with everyone.

"It does say a lot (about the mainly British and Irish players who were at the club last season). Then again, it's football and we're at a high level, so everyone knows there's going to be a lot of competition.

"The main thing is just being as good as you can to each other off the pitch and then when we're on the pitch as competitive as possible.

"I feel that's a really important strength because that's what's got us here so far. I feel like we need to keep that until the end of the season."

Not all of the new signings came speaking good English, so Cho's bilingualism is important.

"I've got a few of the French players I'm pretty close to," he says. "Lucas Gourna (a team-mate in the French age-group teams) speaks fairly good English so it's not too much of a problem with him.

"But Nobel (Mendy) and Robinio (Vaz), they don't speak that good English so sometimes you have to help them out.

"I've got my family not too far from here in Manchester so that's been really helpful, and some of my team-mates live really close by so we always go to each other's (homes) and just chill with each other.

"It's really important off the pitch what you do to be good on the pitch."

If Cho's off-field role is clear, on the field it has been less so.

He may not have had the language barrier to hurdle, but he has had many of the problems his team-mates did joining late in the transfer window, in his case because of what he calls a "roller-coaster" of an on-off transfer. Coach Sergej Jakirovic thinks he has still not yet caught up.

"He's a very quick player so he can run behind," explains Jakirovic. "Maybe sometimes he can better cover the ball, to save the ball (keep possession), at least to win a foul.

"It's also about fitness because his recovery after sprinting is still too long. In his last club (Nice), he was removed from training because he was waiting for a transfer. Ten days he didn't train with the team.

"Now he's healthy, thank God, and everything's on him (to perform)."

Hull have largely used Cho from the bench as a right winger but their best player, Mohamed Belloumi – one of the younger members of the old guard – plays there too. Their next best, Oli McBurnie, is a centre-forward, his other position.

So it was significant for Cho that Jakirovic switched from 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 at Arsenal, giving Cho a first Premier League start alongside McBurnie.

"I need to keep working and stay ready," says Cho, who picked up a minor injury on the back of his first goal. "Wherever the coach wants me to play, I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can to the team.

"(Arsenal) was a great experience. I knew it was going to be tough even before the game.

"But Iit was just trying to make advantage of my colleagues by getting in behind, trying to hurt the opponents with my runs in behind and trying to be a threat every time we had the ball in transition.

"I know I can do better, we can do better as a team always but I feel like there's a lot to take from it."

#2011. Newcastle United vs. Arsenal: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Premier League clash

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 08:14, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:15

Newcastle United will welcome Arsenal to St James' Park in the Premier League on Saturday evening.

Newcastle are 12th in the Premier League table, boasting 12 points from their opening 10 matches of the season, while Arsenal are at the head of the division, five points ahead of second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 5.30pm UK time on Saturday.

The Premier League match between Newcastle and Arsenal will be held at the former's home ground, St James' Park.

The corresponding game last season ended in a 2-1 victory for Arsenal, with Mikel Merino and Gabriel scoring late to secure all three points for the North London outfit.

The Premier League contest will be available on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League for viewers in the UK.

Sky customers can access the Premier League match on Sky Go and on the Sky Sports app, while it is also available via Now TV's Sports membership.

Sky Sports will show highlights, including any goals which have been scored, on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app.

Meanwhile, on Saturday, BBC One's Match of the Day programme will begin at 10.20pm and run until 11.45pm, with highlights of the match also available via that avenue.

Arsenal have won nine and lost one of their 10 Premier League matches this season, with 27 points leaving them five points clear at the top of the division.

Mikel Arteta's side recorded a 1-0 win over Hull City before the November international break, and they have been victorious in their last three matches in all competitions.

The likes of Brighton and Man City will be hoping for a favour from Newcastle in this match, as Arsenal are threatening to pull further clear at the top of the division.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough start to the season for Newcastle, with 12 points leaving them down in 12th spot in the division.

The Magpies entered the November international break off the back of a 1-1 draw with Fulham.

“When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence. You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

“We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and shows grit. We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that.

“We looked unmotivated and lacking edge tonight. Tactically astute, we were miles away and that’s my responsibility. All areas of our performance was disappointing. I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.”

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

The player himself covered his face with his hand before retrieving the ball to get play started again.

Arsenal players wheeled off in celebration, only for Comunicaciones to level things up in the game soon after. Arsenal, though, scored again, and eventually won 3-2 in the first leg of the tie.

"Us defending in a block with looking to break with Slatts (Callum Slattery) and Davis (Keillor-Dunn) and Barry Bannan doesn't really work for us, so we need to be more aggressive, high up the pitch, and expose ourselves. We didn't do that, it'll take time.

"I'll own that in terms of what it looks like but that's where we need to get to.

"We've got to at that point really be on the neck of people and go and get the third goal, not be comfortable thinking two is an easy night for us because you allow a young team to get some momentum and come back into the game."

But as critical as he was of areas of the first-half performance, Challinor was delighted with the spirt he saw in his new players in the second half.

"We've got we've got a group that want to defend right across the board," he said. "We've done some work this week around emergency defending.

"You're not going to get much better than Coops (Liam Cooper), Sil (Swinkels), Dish (Di'Shon Bernard), Yan (Valery) and Rico (Ricardo Santos).

"They want to block, they want to get themselves in the way.

"We were a little bit better second half.

"We had a really good chat at half time. I told them what I felt, we'd just got to make better decisions.

"We've got we've got an experienced group, but some of our decision-making in that last half an hour caused us more problems than it should have.

"If it's a derby, you need to be able to be 100 per cent because Barnsley, at that point, are going for it, are open, and two or three passes, we could have we could have been in a lot more often, and we made the wrong decision at the wrong time.

"Winning's a brilliant habit, but I'm very realistic about the work that needs to be done.

"I never have been a great winner, as daft as that sounds. My job's to be analytical and understand where we get better.

"I want them to enjoy winning. I've said that to them. I want it to be absolutely bouncing because winning's a brilliant feeling and a brilliant habit to get into.

"They found a way when maybe not performed the best. There's loads more to come from this group. My job is to make sure that happens.

"You're always going to be try and be a perfectionist as a football coach. You'll never get to that but that doesn't mean you stop trying."

#2006. Rangers avoid title blip as late own goal breaks Motherwell resistance and Celtic kept within eyeline

In the crisp chill of a late November evening in North Lanarkshire, Rangers required a late deflection to prise three vital Scottish Premiership points from the grasp of a resolute and industrious Motherwell side.

With the contest seemingly bound to end 1-1, a potentially significant blip for the visitors in terms of their title aspirations, Ryan Naderi’s 88th-minute effort struck the unfortunate Martin Moormann and looped past goalkeeper Alex Paulsen, inflicting the cruellest of blows on the Steelmen.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

There seemed an almost ritualistic rhythm to Rangers’ recent visits to Fir Park: waves of possession crashing against a disciplined claret-and-amber breakwater, accompanied by the persistent nagging doubt that dominance without ruthlessness invites punishment.

Derek McInnes’s side were living out that exact cautionary tale on their latest visit before Naderi popped up with a crucial late winner.

For the opening 15 minutes, this contest threatened to become a procession. Rangers monopolised the ball and the opening goal arrived after just eight minutes. Motherwell’s defensive structure momentarily frayed under early pressure, allowing centre-back Emmanuel Fernandez to rise unmarked and head home Kim Min-Su’s corner with disarming simplicity.

At that juncture, Motherwell appeared to be unravelling. Within six minutes of falling behind, Alfred Johansson was forced into an early reshuffle when winger Ibrahim Said limped off injured in visible distress to be replaced by Regan Charles-Cook.

Rangers sensed blood. Naderi probed tirelessly, Djeidi Gassama repeatedly cut inside off the left flank to test the Steelmen defence, and Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was called upon to produce a string of top-class saves to prevent the visitors from establishing an unassailable cushion.

However, Scottish football rarely rewards aesthetic superiority alone. Having weathered the initial storm without conceding a second, the hosts summoned an equaliser from their first corner of the evening in the 21st minute. Emmanuel Longelo rolled a clever short pass to Tom Sparrow, whose curling delivery into the penalty area found Jake Girdwood-Reich entirely unmarked. The Australian defender needed no second invitation, sweeping a composed finish past Ivor Pandur to restore parity against the run of play.

That subtly altered the psychological temperature inside Fir Park. While Rangers continued to dictate proceedings, racking up nearly 20 attempts on goal, their lack of cutting edge in the final third was glaring. Before the interval, Paulsen defied the visitors once more with a superb reflex stop from Nico Raskin in the 41st minute.

McInnes’ men pressed forward with renewed urgency after a stern half-time team talk. Seven minutes into the second half, Dan Neil drifted into a pocket of space on the edge of the area and drilled a low effort that whistled agonisingly past the post.

Visible frustration began to creep into Rangers’ ranks passing the hour mark as a combination of misplaced passes and poor finishing drew audible groans from the packed away end.

Sensing his team’s grip on the contest loosening, McInnes turned to his bench in the 69th minute, introducing summer signing Kevin Kelsy in place of Gassama to add a greater physical presence in attack alongside Naderi. There was little immediate improvement. Badredine Bouanani raced down the right flank and cut the ball back for Neil, whose shot sailed high and wide.

Motherwell were looking increasingly comfortable and Tawanda Maswanhise tested Pandur from distance as the home side sensed an opportunity to claim something more substantial than a point.

Findlay Curtis was introduced for Rangers and almost made an immediate impact, delivering an excellent cross towards the back post which Naderi was unable to turn home from close range.

Then came another extraordinary intervention from Paulsen. Curtis' effort appeared to have beaten the keeper, who could only palm the ball into the path of Sterling. However, Paulsen recovered magnificently to divert the right-back’s follow-up onto the crossbar. It was a remarkable piece of goalkeeping and, by this stage, it seemed entirely possible that the home side would clinch a share of the spoils.

With two minutes remaining, Rangers finally found the breakthrough their territorial dominance had threatened to deliver. Naderi got his effort away, but Moormann intervened and inadvertently diverted the ball beyond his own goalkeeper. The unfortunate centre-back could do little about the decisive deflection, but the consequences were devastating for Motherwell.

The travelling Rangers support erupted, relief and celebration combining in equal measure. For McInnes, it was a precious late reward for a side that had made unnecessarily hard work of a match they might have settled long before the closing stages.

The victory extends Rangers' unbeaten run in all competitions to 13 matches and ensures they remain in touch with Celtic, moving back within four points of the league leaders with a game in hand.

#2003. Nations League quarter-final draw: Why England are favourites to win the tournament

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:00

England should be seen as the favourites to win the UEFA Nations League ahead of the quarter-final draw, a former Three Lions striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Thomas Tuchel's side will learn their knockout fate on Friday morning when the draw for the last eight is held, and England head into the ceremony as one of the four seeded teams courtesy of finishing first in League A Group 3.

The Three Lions unexpectedly pipped world and European champions Spain to top spot courtesy of an engrossing 3-2 win over La Roja on Sunday, ending an unparalleled 43-game unbeaten run for Luis de la Fuente's side.

England will meet one of Belgium, Netherlands or Norway in the quarter-finals, while France, Portugal and Germany represent the other three Group A winners going for glory.

Despite the strength of the draw, former England striker Mark Hateley believes that Tuchel's men have made themselves the favourites to win the trophy for the first time, and also reserved special praise foe the goalkeeping heroics of James Trafford.

Asked if England are leading the charge for Nations League stardom, Hateley replied: "100%. That's the best I've seen England, or any team, play over a period of, say, 60 minutes.

"They were incredible: high press, press, press, press, going man for man, confident enough to go man for man at the back against the world champions, allowing your midfield players to jump up with the strikers.

“It was tremendous to watch, the very best we've seen from an England side for many, many years, honestly. It was superb. We went to 3-0, rightly so, and Spain never had a shot. Their first was 50 minutes in, in the second half.

“Trafford must have thought 'this was a goddamn easy game.' The only time I think he was at fault was his starting position for the penalty, when Anderson brought the boy down. If his starting position had been higher, I think he'd have made the interception. That would be my only fault for the goalkeeper.

“If you’re a shot stopper, you’re a shot stopper - it’s just the other side of his game, where you're reading it and where you should be, playing as that sweeper.

"With the way we were pressing, the only ball really on for Spain was a ball in behind into the last third, which was empty for long periods. There was nobody there where I thought he could have been. But those are the things you pick up on and learn from.”

England have only ever competed in the Nations League knockout stages once before in the inaugural 2018-19 edition, when they reached the finals courtesy of beating Spain and Croatia to first place in their group.

However, at a time when the Nations League Finals only comprised four teams, Gareth Southgate's side fell to a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands in the semi-finals, meaning that they are still awaiting their first knockout-phase win in the tournament.

England could only place third in the group stage of the 2020-21 tournament, before an embarrassing relegation to League B in the 2022-23 edition, although they swiftly returned to the top tier.

In the current format, England's record of five wins, one loss and 19 goals scored represented their best-ever performance in the group stage of the Nations League, fuelling the belief that the Three Lions can finally end their trophy drought in 2027.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.

#2002. Fabian Hurzeler makes Brajan Gruda and Brighton claim amid Jurgen Klopp and transfer update

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler admits it was not always easy for Brajan Gruda at Brighton.

Gruda joined Brighton in 2024 for £25m from Bundesliga club Mainz and showed glimpses of his potential with the Seagulls.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The German playmaker made 43 appearances and claimed four goals with eight assists but struggled to nail down a regular starting position.

Right wing and the No 10 spot is Gruda's preferred role and he was regularly behind the likes of Yankuba Minteh, Diego Gomez and Georginio Rutter in the pecking order.

Gruda joined RB Leipzig on loan for the second part of last term and then agreed to a season-long loan last summer.

The 22-year-old has impressed in the Bundesliga and has five goals and eight assists in total for Martín Demichelis' Leipzig, who are fourth in the German top flight.

Gruda also dazzled for Germany last week as he scored a fine individual goal on his full debut against Serbia and then claimed two assists and netted a goal in Germany's 5-0 win against The Netherlands. Brighton's Bart Verbruggen was in goal for the Dutch.

Germany boss Jurgen Klopp heaped praise on Gruda. "He's a fantastic player who loves to take people on," said the former Liverpool manager. "And he hasn't yet fulfilled his potential."

Gruda is contracted with Brighton until 2028 and his loan at Liepzig is believed to have an obligation to buy, with certain conditions.

“The obligation to buy for Brajan Gruda will be activated in 2027 due to accounting reasons," posted German transfer expert Florian Plettenberg. "The total package for RB Leipzig will amount to €30m."

He also stated that Bayern Munich are keeping a close eye on the situation.

Gruda's development has left many Brighton fans hoping for a return - especially with the uncertainty surrounding Minteh, who almost joined Liverpool last summer.

"I'm also full of praise for Gruda," said Fabian Hurzeler to Sussex World ahead Sunday's trip to Hull City.

"Because when I see him playing, I see a great development. He's doing the basic things well. I think one thing that Jürgen always mentioned is to make him run back, to make him defend.

"I think this will always be the key for his game. Then in possession, he always has the quality to beat an opponent."

Asked why it did not work out for him at Brighton, Hurzeler told Sussex World: "Again, he was very young with us. For us, it was always important to give him more game minutes.

"He had a lot of competition when Minteh was playing in this position, Diego Gomez was in this position. So it was not that easy for him to get those game minutes.

"Then he made the move to Leipzig, where he had more and more game minutes.

"Especially with these young players, I think you see brilliantly now with our young players, if they get game minutes, if they have this trust and confidence, then they are capable of doing really good things.

"I think that was the only issue here with him, that he didn't have this confidence and these game minutes, and now he can really express himself."

Hurzeler is though delighted by his improvement and believes working with Klopp is a "good fit" for Gruda. The Brighton boss was however coy on whether Gruda will be seen in Brighton colours again.

"It's a joy to watch him,” he said to Sussex World. “I'm really happy to see him playing like this. I think it's a good fit with Jürgen.

"I think that Jürgen really gets this belief into his players and therefore it was a joy to watch Germany playing this week.

"To see them chasing as a team, to see them doing counter-pressing, gegenpressing, and that's really good.

"I'm really happy for Brajan, so let's see how the future will be."

#2000. Ronaldinho makes return at age of 46: Brazil legend plays full first-half for Italian third-tier team and hints he may play again despite 'publicity stunt' criticism

Published: 15:51 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 15:52 EST, 15 November 2026

Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.

The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar announced his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.

Having enjoyed retirement for 11 years, he shocked world football by agreeing a surprise transfer to Serie C outfit Ravenna, where he was set to undertake a marketing role.

It was initially understood that he would not be making a playing return, but the Brazil legend laced up his boots on Sunday and played a part in his side's opening goal.

Ravenna's honorary vice president Ariedo Braida said in June that the World Cup winner would regrettably not be able to play for the club due to his age.

But it appears that went up in smoke, with Ronaldinho playing 45 minutes on his return in the league clash – despite his move being dubbed a publicity stunt by the club.

Brazil icon Ronaldinho has made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46

He played the first-half of the game, playing a role in the first goal for his new side

He helped set up Giulio Donati's opening goal of the match, and raced across the field to mob the goal scorer as he celebrated.

He started the game, playing the first-half before being replaced by Matteo Maggio. Before his substitution, he embraced the fans in the stands at the interval.

The icon hinted there could be more games to come, however.

He told Sky Italia after the game: 'It went by too fast, that has always been football for me.

'Is this my last one? I don't know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.

'It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.'

Ronaldinho has also become a shareholder in the club.

During his illustrious career, he won the World Cup, a Champions League, two LaLiga titles and a Serie A trophy before hanging up his boots in 2015.

He also won a string of individual accolades including the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and FIFA World Player of the Year in 2004 and 2005.

#1997. Bologna vs Udinese - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 09:03, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:08

Aiming to pick up where they left off before the break, Bologna will host Serie A's bottom side when Udinese visit Stadio Dall'Ara on Sunday.

After a sticky start, both clubs have already changed coaches, and the Rossoblu's new boss has sparked a surge up the standings.

Since Raffaele Palladino's arrival midway through September, Bologna have been a team transformed, winning five games from six and climbing towards the European places.

The Emilian club signed off for the international break with a run of four consecutive wins, with the highlight being a 4-2 victory over AC Milan at San Siro.

Last time out, the Rossoblu's revival continued in the Derby dell'Emilia against Parma, as their hosts were swiftly reduced to 10 men and ultimately suffered a 2-1 defeat.

So, having won none of their first five games during the short-lived Domenico Tedesco era, Bologna are now one of Serie A's form sides.

However, Palladino must still work on their awful home record, which stretches back through most of last season; so far this term, they have claimed five points from a possible 15 at the Dall'Ara.

Either home or away, Udinese have picked up just one from their last nine matches and are therefore stuck at the foot of the table.

The Bianconeri have put a meagre five points on the board so far, slumping into an unexpected crisis.

Safe mid-table finishers in back-to-back seasons under Kosta Runjaic, this campaign has completely unravelled, and even a change of coach has yet to produce results.

Just before the break, new boss Paolo Zanetti lost his first game against former club Venezia, with Udinese going down 2-1 in a crucial battle at the bottom.

Now, desperately needing some success, Zanetti must meet Palladino for the seventh time in management - to date, the pair have three wins apiece.

Unfortunately for fans of the Friulani, recent history is not on their side: they have won none of the last five meetings with Bologna, failing to even score in each of the last three.

Though Bologna will be without injured trio Jay Enem, Juan Miranda and Emil Holm, left-winger Nicolo Cambiaghi has resumed training after leaving Italy's UEFA Nations League camp.

Having impressed in the Azzurri's win over France, Cambiaghi has overcome a minor ankle problem and should start alongside Federico Bernadeschi in the final third.

The latter has previously scored four goals against Udinese, finding the net as a substitute in both of the last two meetings.

Bernardeschi and Samuel Mbangula - who recently hit a hat-trick at San Siro - are the hosts' joint-top Serie A scorers with three goals each; Jurgen Ekkelenkamp has netted three times for Udinese.

The visitors must travel without Nicolo Bertola, who has suffered a thigh injury in training and joins Idrissa Gueye on the sidelines.

In better news for Zanetti, David Alaba could return from his latest layoff, while Nicolo Zaniolo is available after withdrawing from the Italy squad for personal reasons.

#1995. Crawley Town earn first home win in league since March after determined display against Fleetwood

The win came in Kevin Blackwell’s first game as permanent manager after his appointment earlier this week.

A goal in either half from Kai Jennings, Pemi Aderoju and a resolute back-line performance earned Crawley a deserved win.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It takes the Reds to within three points from safety, with as many games in hand against 22nd-placed Rochdale.

Reds made a fast start to the first half and took the lead in the fourth minute through Jennings, following Kellan Gordon’s cross from a darting run down the right wing.

Fleetwood, Arsenal’s conquerors and League Cup quarter-finalists, failed to clear their lines on the edge of the six-yard box and Jennings pounced on their indecision to smash home into the roof of the net.

New Reds centre back Ben Heneghan blocked a well-hit shot from range in the Cod Army’s first effort on goal in the ninth minute.

Vito Mannone calmy claimed Jake Batty’s left-wing cross to dispel Fleetwood as the away side got a foothold in the game and started to up the pressure, shortly before Reds nervily dealt with an Andy Cannon cross.

On the 15-minute mark Aderoju found himself through one-on-one but shot straight into the welcoming arms of Fleetwood keeper Jay Lynch.

Mannone was called upon to punch clear a couple of searching Fleetwood crosses into the box and lifted the pressure of his side in an open context.

Dylan Mogan nearly put the Reds 2-0 up on the half hour, he tricked his way past the Fleetwood right-back but curling shot from the edge of the box clipped the post and went out for a goal kick.

Just before the break Fleetwood’s Aaron Loupal-Bi got into a good position on the left after a one-two but his tame effort along the ground was collected by Mannone.

Reds flew out the traps to double their lead within a minute of the restart, Morgan stormed through Fleetwood’s midfield and slotted Aderoju in on-goal and the big target man rifled a left-foot shot into the back of the net.

The visitors responded by almost pulling one back from a curling shot from the edge of the box and then hit the post moments afterwards.

Reds first chance of the second half fell to Aderoju who rose well but headed just wide from Gordon’s good right-side delivery.

Fleetwood gave themselves a lifeline thanks to substitute Will Davies’ firing a shot past Mannone from the middle of the penalty area to give the travelling fans behind the goal a reason to cheer.

Reds matched Fleetwood as the physicality grew as the half wore on and dug in to match their opponents.

Fleetwood substitute Lewis McCann stung the gloves of Mannone and produced a match-winning save from the big Italian who’s clean sheet was hard-earned.

Duke-McKenna had the chance to seal the points for the Reds at the end after chopping back onto his left foot down the right side, but his curled shot was parried away by Lynch.

Crawley are back at Broadfield in league action again this Tuesday (November 24) as they aim to climb out of the drop-zone in a tough test against high-flying Barnet.

#1994. Sergej Jakirovic on Hull City taking a risk following Brighton and Hove Albion blueprint

The Seagulls started the 21st Century in English football's fourth tier with no history of challenging at the top of the pyramid and no home, but are now second in the Premier League, fifth in the Europa Conference League and looking good for it. They will come to East Yorkshire on Sunday looking to end Hull's unbeaten start to the season at home.

Although they have not won since August, the Tigers are also punching above their weight, 13th in the Premier League and crucially with more points than games played after coming up via the play-offs.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hull signed 18 players in the summer, 14 of whom were under the age of 25, and another 14 new to the Premier League.

“We have to speak about them because it is not now by accident,” said Hull coach Jakirovic. “They are performing even better every game.

“They have very big confidence, an excellent coach (Fabian Hurzeler), system. This club has a spine and very good players – young players with potential.

“If your energy is below 100 per cent you don't have a chance against them.

“They sold a few good players but they have good scouting. They always bring in young potential players. They pay money for them, then they try to develop these players and then sell again. It is a great system.”

“Sometimes you cannot afford better players, more expensive players, but I think that we brought young players with good potential,” he said.

“Now it's about developing and how we can improve them because this is a very big step for some of them.

“Especially if you stay in the league, then you have more money, you can invest, you can add more quality players.

“It's about vision. It's about strategy. This is everything with Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth – they showed already how one club who is new in the league can be successful.

“This is maybe an example of what we need to do.”

Not many of Hull's new 18 have made much impact in the Premier League – yet. Some were always going to take time, and others will not come off at all.

“We have some examples here who joined us too late after pre-season, then you start to play,” acknowledged Jakirovic. “(You pick up) one injury, recovery, second injury. Now it's difficult to get back into the team – especially the first XI.

“They need time and they have to be patient and work very hard every day. So this is risky.”

Nobel Mendy is fit again after an international break where Hull had a large number of players representing their countries, and Jakirovic watching closely to see how they performed.

“We had 12 players in the building (during the break),” he said. “But we had two good sessions before Thursday when we were finally all together. everyone got back healthy.

“Now it's about fatigue, it's about condition. On Saturday we will decide who will play.

“I tried to watch every game (his internationals played) and if I cannot watch, Josh (Marris, senior analyst) will put it on our computer. Even Qatar v Australia (which centre-back Lucas Herrington played in), even under-21 games, Greece, Norway, with Jens (Hjerto-Dahl).”

#1993. Barcelona vs. Villarreal: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 09:23, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:23

Barcelona will resume their 2026-27 La Liga campaign with a home fixture against Villarreal on Sunday afternoon.

Hansi Flick's side are currently top of the La Liga table, boasting a record of 11 wins and one defeat from their 12 matches to collect 33 points, which has left them three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid at this stage of proceedings.

Barcelona have won their last three games in all competitions, including a 2-1 success over Atletico Madrid in their last fixture before the November international break.

Villarreal, meanwhile, have a record of four wins, three draws and five defeats from their 12 league matches this season to collect 15 points.

The Yellow Submarine are currently eighth in the division, three points behind sixth-placed Sevilla.

Here, Sports Mole looks at the head-to-head record between Barcelona and Villarreal ahead of their clash at Camp Nou this weekend.

Barcelona have tackled Villarreal on 58 occasions throughout history, and they comfortably lead the head-to-head record, posting 36 wins to Villarreal's 12, while there have also been 10 draws.

Lionel Messi is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having found the back of the net on 16 occasions against Villarreal during his time at Barcelona, while Neymar is second on nine.

As for the Yellow Submarine, former Manchester United and Atletico Madrid star Diego Forlan is their leading goalscorer against Barcelona, having netted five times against the Catalan outfit during his Villarreal career.

In La Liga, there have been 52 meetings, with Barcelona's winning 32 times to Villarreal's 11, while the points have been shared on nine occasions in Spain's top flight.

Villarreal incredibly recorded a 5-3 victory away to Barcelona in January 2024 and 3-2 win in May 2025, either side of a 5-1 triumph for the Catalan team in September 2024.

However, they were most recently downed 2-0 by La Blaugrana at Estadio de la Ceramica in December 2025, with centre-back Renato Veiga being sent off for a reckless tackle on Lamine Yamal, who went on to score the second for Hansi Flick's side.

Villarreal's last three wins over Barcelona have all come away from home, and they have not actually managed to beat the Catalan side in front of their own supporters since October 2007.

Barcelona's dominance in this fixture is perhaps best highlighted by the fact that they have won 12 of the last 15 La Liga meetings between the two clubs, even if Villarreal have enjoyed strong spells such as when they recorded three straight victories between April 2007 and March 2008.

The last meeting between the two sides took place at Camp Nou in February 2026, with Barcelona recording a 4-1 win.

Barcelona will now be looking to post a third straight victory over Villarreal.

#1991. Chelsea 1 Leeds United 4: Whites avenge cup exits in style by tearing Xabi Alonso’s Blues apart

Leeds United avenged the two cup defeats they suffered at Chelsea’s hands with a stunning 4-1 victory over their old rivals at Stamford Bridge.

Having been edged out by the Blues at the semi-final stage of the FA Cup in April, Leeds were subjected to a 6-3 Carabao Cup mauling by Xabi Alonso’s men in September.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

On this occasion, however, it was Daniel Farke’s men inflicting the damage. Emmanuel Emegha fired the hosts ahead, but Noah Okafor goals either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty and a late Brenden Aaronson finish gave Leeds a Premier League win that will go down in the history books.

Chelsea sought to assume authority from the get-go, with Cole Palmer driving at the heart of the Leeds midfield inside the opening minute. The hosts may have been straight on the offensive, but Leeds soon made it clear they would not be content with one-way traffic.

Jayden Bogle and Sean Longstaff both made headway down the right-hand side, sending in crosses that were not capitalised upon.

The opening exchanges played out in a fast and furious manner, with robust challenges stoking the fires of a historic rivalry. Chelsea had the early edge, although referee Michael Oliver had no interest in appeals for a penalty when Tarik Muharemovic challenged Emmanuel Emegha inside the box.

Leeds handled Chelsea’s ventures forward well, mostly limiting the Blues to speculative efforts. Josh Acheamping, Morgan Rogers and Estevao all pulled the trigger from distance, yet little was asked of James Trafford between the Leeds sticks.

At the other end, Leeds continued to make inroads on the right. James Justin whipped a cross over for Calvert-Lewin, who struggled to generate power but did hit the crossbar with his looped header.

Leeds’ focus soon shifted to the left, where Gudmundsson started to flex his attacking muscles. He made an incisive dart into the box and went to ground under close attention from Estevao, although the referee paid no attention to penalty appeals.

Leeds’ left wing-back then picked out Calvert-Lewin and saw the England international force a strong hand from Emiliano Martinez with a headed effort.

The visitors looked to be moving through the gears but just as the tide was turning, Chelsea drew first blood. Justin and Nico Elvedi both failed to stop the advancement of Rogers, who fed Emegha and saw the frontman beat Trafford at his near post with a blasted finish.

Leeds bit back almost immediately, levelling proceedings within three minutes of the opener. Calvert-Lewin contested a long ball with Wesley Fofana before picking up the scraps and releasing Okafor, who jinked his way into space and rifled across Martinez.

With the wind behind their sails, Leeds came close to overturning the deficit via their equaliser’s creator. Calvert-Lewin met a Muharemovic cross and his deft flick came agonisingly close to finding the bottom corner.

Farke’s men continued applying pressure in the closing stages of the first half and Ao Tanaka was unfortunate to see a rasping rocket of a shot deflected before it could cause Martinez any trouble.

Gudmundsson then danced his way into an opportunity before poking harmlessly wide of Martinez’s right-hand post.

The next chance fell to Tanaka, who pushed the ball out of his feet but could only force a straightforward save with a shot straight down Martinez’s throat.

Leeds did have the ball in the back of the net on the stroke of half-time, although Justin was clearly offside before he delivered for Muharemovic to finish. When the half-time whistle did blow, it was Leeds firmly in the driving seat.

The second half started as the first ended, with Leeds in the ascendency. There were early appeals for a penalty when Calvert-Lewin tangled with Martinez, but Oliver was again dismissive of protests.

Tanaka then stretched to get on the end of a cross from deep, steering just off target as pressure piled on Chelsea.

Having seen their protests ignored mere minutes earlier, Leeds saw Oliver point to the spot when Rogers was judged to have handled a Muharemovic shot. After a lengthy VAR check, the decision was stuck by and Calvert-Lewin buried the spot-kick.

Chelsea responded by putting their front foot forward and Rogers forced Trafford down to his left with a low drive from distance.

However, it was Leeds who struck next and sent the the travelling supporters into a frenzy. After Chelsea failed to clear their lines after a long throw, Ethan Ampadu’s deflected cross was hammered home by Okafor in emphatic fashion.

Somewhat predictably, Chelsea surged back into the driving seat as they looked for a way back into a game getting away from them. Much to the frustration of the home supporters, their spell of control yielded little more than occasional half-chances.

There were sharp inhales of breath when Rogers arrowed a free-kick goalwards from a tight angle, but it dipped over the crossbar with Trafford at full stretch.

Many of Chelsea’s supporters were already heading out to beat the traffic when Aaronson capped an astonishing afternoon, wriggling through a creaking defence before steering a fourth past Martinez.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But the hosts defended resolutely to earn only their second win in the league this campaign – and their first at home since March.

And Blackwell, while pleased to earn all three points, is keen to quickly build on the positive result.

He said: “It's always great when you win, isn't it? And it's been a long time coming this season, so we will enjoy it but know that we've got a tough game against Barnet on Tuesday [November 24].

“It's just that process now of games coming and hopefully trying to improve the squad and improve the team, and hopefully we get some more results at home.”

Despite the win, Crawley remain bottom of League Two but are unbeaten in their last three games.

Blackwell referenced the high stakes currently at play each time the Reds are in action.

He said: “When you're down where we are, if it can go wrong, it will go wrong. So, we've got to be careful. We don't take risks in some areas. Make sure we fight our socks off. It's as simple as that.

“We're in a dogfight. I want plenty of dogs fighting for us. And you saw today, everybody was fighting for the cause, and that's what I want. They've got to be proud to be a professional footballer, proud to be at Crawley Town, and proud to work for me.”

Blackwell added: “I said to the boys as we went out, ‘this is Crawley Town, this is our home. I don't want anybody coming here thinking, ‘oh, we're playing Crawley, it’s nice and easy’.

“I want them to go back thinking, ‘we've got to get on the bus and do a five-hour trip after being at Crawley’. That's what I want. And I think today, Fleetwood will get on the bus and think, ‘that was a tough one at Crawley today’.”

As the Reds boss alluded to, his side are back in action at the Broadfield against second-placed Barnet on Tuesday night.

#1987. Striker Che Adams says Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli is big on the small details... 'he loves his FaceTime calls'

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be big on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the new man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli

Striker Adams says Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’

Hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’

John McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

‘He said to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very important to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ said Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’

#1981. Arsenal suffer huge early injury blows for Man City, Real Madrid as Mikel Arteta gives Bukayo Saka, Martin Zubimendi updates

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 10:00

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has revealed that Bukayo Saka will spend another four weeks on the sidelines with the quadriceps injury he sustained against Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Saka's injury occurred in the first half of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Bundesliga champions on October 21, and Arteta immediately conceded at full time that the winger's problem looked severe.

Reports emerging soon after stated that Saka would miss between six and eight weeks, although Arsenal have been loath to put an exact timeframe on the Englishman's recovery just yet.

However, speaking to the media ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Newcastle United, Arteta admitted that Saka was only halfway into his recovery process and would spend the full eight weeks out.

"We had another test. It looks like it’s going to be an eight week injury more or less. He’s four weeks in now," the Spaniard told reporters.

Saka missing another four weeks means that the 25-year-old is set to sit out another seven matches across all competitions, including a number of heavyweight fixtures.

Arsenal host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League next Tuesday, before ending the month with a clash of the titans against Manchester City in the Premier League.

Saka is also expected to miss matches with Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in early December, and he will most likely be unavailable for the visit of Bournemouth on December 13 too.

However, the attacker could be fit to make his comeback against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on December 20, until when Noni Madueke and Max Dowman will provide cover.

Dowman will serve the third of his three-game domestic suspension against Newcastle this weekend, but Madueke has earned numerous plaudits in recent weeks, having scored against Slavia Prague in the Champions League before firing the effort that led to Martin Odegaard's winner against Hull City.

Saka will likely be one of two core members of Arsenal's title-winning team to miss matches against Tottenham and Real Madrid, as Arteta also delivered negative news on Martin Zubimendi.

The midfielder appeared to hurt his hamstring in Spain's 3-2 Nations League defeat to England during the international break, and he also faces around a month on the sidelines.

"He has a problem in his hamstring. The scan shows there is an injury there he will be out for a few weeks," Arteta added on Zubimendi.

However, the 27-year-old is yet to start a Premier League game this season and was always expected to lose out to Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes at St James' Park tomorrow.

Arsenal are five points clear at the top of the Premier League table heading into gameweek 11 and are searching for their fourth successive win over Newcastle in the top flight.

#1978. Bradford City boss Michael Duff on 'big turning point' versus Doncaster Rovers plus praise for Nick Powell and two substitutes

A low-key derby came to life in the final half-hour after Nick Powell – making his first league start of the campaign – headed the hosts’ in front on 55 minutes.

Simkin repelled the attempts of City to make it 2-0 and Rovers levelled on 74 minutes, courtesy of an overhead kick from Jordan Thomas as City conceded a spectacular goal from the visitors’ first effort on target for the second successive league game, following Joe Low’s opener for Huddersfield Town at BD8 on October 31.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Soon after, substitute Humphrys, impressive when he entered the fray, fired the hosts back in front following perceptive work from fellow replacement Will Swan.

That looked to be that, only for City to switch off in the fifth minute of stoppage time from Robbie Gotts’ corner, allowing Sean Grehan to secure a precious point for lowly Rovers.

Duff, whose side moved up to sixth, said: “I thought the performance was good. We scored twice, the only thing we didn’t do was get a two-goal lead.

"At 1-0, the big turning point is probably the goalkeeper save. If it gets to 2-0, I think we win the game.

"But when there’s only one goal in it, you’re always on the edge of your seat. We just switched off from a corner in the 95th minute which is unlike us.

"They’ve had two shots on target and scored two goals. Jon (McCracken) has not made a save and one of them is an overhead kick again.

"You take that out of it and there were a lot of good things. We looked a real goal threat against another team that’s come and completely changed the way they normally play.

"The positive is that we looked like we had a few more ideas and looked a real goal threat.

"I thought we were pretty much on top for most of the game. Even from the moment we got the second goal until they scored, it wasn’t like we sat in and it was wave after wave.

"If you play every week and they’re only having two shots – and they’re not scoring from an overhead kick that’s very similar to the Huddersfield. That won’t happen all season.

"No one likes conceding in the 95th minute but we should have won the game.

"There’s disappointment in the dressing room but I don’t mind it. It’s a good thing to walk out with.

"Then Monday is your evidence about what was good and what we need to tidy up.

"It’s hard to prep when you don’t know what the opposition are going to do at the minute. The fact they changed it, we saw it and reacted really well.

"Grant (McCann) is normally a possession-based manager and didn't try and play out at all today, but that's part of the challenge.”

Powell found the net for the ninth time this season and continued his excellent start to the campaign.

On the veteran striker, Duff, whose side welcome former club Barnsley – now bottom – on Tuesday, continued: “I was really pleased for him. he had to work hard to get to that.

"I thought Stephen Humphrys was good when he came on as well, so again we've scored two goals, we've got two nines on the pitch that both scored.

"Obviously Jake Beesley missed out through injury but he'll be back at some point, so there's good competition for places in that part of the pitch.

“Swanny’s (Will Swan) came on and has been involved and impacted the game well.”

The game saw Josh Neufville make his first-team return after two months out with hamstring trouble.

Duff added: "We probably could have got a little bit more out of Josh but you've got to think of the bigger picture. Powelly and Josh will be better for the minutes in them as well.”

#1977. Formation tweak and a monkey off their back - Five things we learned from Crawley Town's big win over Fleetwood

There was a drastic change in formation as the Reds moved to a back three with Ben Heneghan in the middle of the back three with Josh Flint and Charlie Barker either side. Blackwell also decided to field an extra striker with Pemi Aderoju and Danilo Orsi leading the line.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Playing two strikers from the very start is something fans have been crying out for with it being a rarity this season for two strikers to start from the outset with the Reds typically bringing on a second striker towards the end of a game.

It evidently paid off not just in terms of the result but the performance. Orsi is a player who needs service; he isn’t a target man and he isn’t someone whose strong suit is running in behind, so having Aderoju alongside him only compliments him and ultimately brings the best out of each other's game, especially if Crawley continue to play direct.

This win over Fleetwood is Crawley’s first home league since Colin Kazim-Richards first game in charge at the end of March, which was eight months ago.

To hang on to that lead at the end was crucial. Having not had a home league win this season, that would have played on the minds of the players and it was certainly felt in the crowd.

But to now overcome that hurdle, the Reds can really look to make the Broadfield Stadium a fortress going forward.

The Reds seemed to have a lot more fight with a real intensity to the way they played, an element of their game which Blackwell alluded to in his post-match interview also.

They had a lot of time to prepare for today’s game having had no game last weekend, and so that would have allowed not only more time to work on tactical elements of the game, but also their fitness and sharpness and that certainly came across today.

The Reds won a lot of their aerial duels and were convincing in their tackles and challenges across the pitch, showing a real togetherness amongst the players who were all fighting for each other out on that pitch, which is crucial if they want to get out of the position they are in.

Not only was it Crawley’s first home league win of the season, but it also continued their unbeaten run in the league since Blackwell arrived. It started with a 1-1 draw against Tranmere Rovers before a 0-1 win on the road against Oldham Athletic.

Something which Blackwell has reiterated in a number of interviews is full focus on the league, and that focus has proven itself in the results and now it’s all about keeping that run going and building momentum.

The Reds looked very well organised and structured both in and out of position, rarely being caught out in the transition. Blackwell’s teams over the years have been known for being disciplined and cohesive, and that is starting to show in this Crawley side who defended very resolutely in today’s games.

Particularly with the way Crawley have played under Blackwell, they won’t dominate large proportions of the games and today was a prime example.

Both teams had different spells of pressure and dominance throughout the game, with Crawley being the ones to capitalise with two early goals at the start of each half.

#1975. Burnley vs Blackburn Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 10:04

Burnley play host to rivals Blackburn Rovers looking for the win that would ensure that they avoid being cut adrift in the relegation zone.

At a time when the Clarets sit in 22nd position in the Championship table, Rovers return after the international break in 13th place.

When Burnley stormed into a 4-1 lead at Cardiff City earlier this month, Fabio Celestini would have been confident that he was recording his first win as head coach that would also kick-start the club's season.

Instead, a 29-minute capitulation that resulted in a 5-4 defeat in South Wales has left relegation feeling increasingly likely, even though the season is only just under a third of the way complete.

Burnley remain on 10 points from 15 matches, their only success coming at fellow strugglers Watford, and they are already five points adrift of safety.

Although an upturn in fortunes would see them quickly haul themselves back into contention to avoid the drop, conceding 31 goals - the worst defensive record in the Championship - will not fill supporters with confidence.

Five of Burnley's seven Championship games at Turf Moor this season have ended in draws, but they remain the only team in the division without a home victory.

As for Blackburn, they have an interim management team in place after Tony Mowbray stood down from his position earlier this week due to health issues.

Rovers sit 11 points above their fierce rivals in the standings, the pre-season expectation having been that the points difference would be close to the exact opposite at this stage of the campaign.

Nevertheless, Blackburn have won five of their last nine fixtures in the second tier to keep them in the hunt for a playoff spot.

The 2-1 victory over West Ham United in their last outing made it five wins from eight matches at Ewood Park.

However, Rovers have prevailed in just one of their seven away fixtures, a 1-0 success at Bristol City on October 13.

Celestini will inevitably make changes to his Burnley XI, with Max Alleyne and Josh Cullen among those who could return in defence and midfield.

Goalkeeper Max Weiss may potentially be handed a recall between the sticks in place of Gregoire Coubert, while Zeki Amdouni could start on the left flank.

However, Connor Roberts starts a three-game ban, a consequence of an incident at the end of the Cardiff game that led to retrospective punishment.

Despite Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds taking the reins from Mowbray, the Blackburn XI will look similar from the victory over West Ham.

However, second-choice goalkeeper Aynsley Pears is expected to deputise for Balazs Toth, who suffered a finger injury while on international duty with Hungary.

If the likes of Mathias Jorgensen and Ryoya Morishita overcome injuries in time for this fixture, they will likely be named on the substitutes' bench at best.

Weiss; Walker, Ekdal, Alleyne, Pires; Hatate, Cullen; Ramazani, Edwards, Amdouni; Hountondji

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:

Pears; Beyuku, Carter, McLoughlin, Pickering; Morsy, Montgomery; Fevrier, Cantwell, Afolayan; Gudjohnsen

With Burnley struggling for wins and Blackburn having to adapt with Mowbray in charge, this points to a game where both teams would be happy to avoid a defeat. Therefore, we anticipate a low-scoring draw being played out at Turf Moor.

#1974. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admits his newlook team need to deliver sooner rather than later

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a new style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

Asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he said: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  says his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

‘Some new faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’

McGinn also said that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most important part.

‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager said: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

But the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli

‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’

City suffered a wretched derby loss to Huddersfield Town, while Rovers were eviscerated at MK Dons, with another ghastly experience seven days later at Kidderminster Harriers, in the FA Cup, compounding their woes.

The fuse for a hitherto pretty quiet derby was lit by an on-pitch fracas involving Kieran Morgan and George Broadbent in the second period, with both benches clashing - and Duff and McCann copping bookings in the process.

It was the precursor to a riproaring final quarter. McCann was the one smiling at the death.

Rovers’ winger Jordan Thomas cancelled out Nick Powell’s 55th-minute opener with a fantastic overhead kick on 74 minutes.

But the visitors then suffered dismay four minutes later when substitute Stephen Humphrys drilled home an emphatic winner.

There was time for a final twist in the fifth minute of stoppage-time when Sean Grehan headed home unmarked following Robbie Gotts’ corner. It was not the sort of concession that Duff likes.

Morgan and Powell were handed their first league starts of the campaign for Bradford, while Josh Neufville, out since September 19 with hamstring trouble, was a significant returnee.

Keighley’s Matty Pearson was a noteworthy inclusion for Rovers, in his first league start since September 6 and only his second in 2026-27 following a calf injury and double hernia operation.

A rusty challenge inside the first 25 seconds on Powell saw Pearson cop a quick-fire yellow card, placing him on a tightrope for the rest of the game.

City had slightly the better of it in a low-incident first half, which smacked of classic derby fare. The goalless scoreline at the interval was just fine given recent events for Rovers, that said.

They were diligent and competitive, which was a step in the right direction given Aggborough and Stadium MK and a scruffy sort of game also suited them in the circumstances.

Rare as they were, scares on goal were provided by those in claret and amber, who boasted 67.6 per cent possession.

Powell planted a meaty header wide under pressure following an inviting cross from Neufville, who fancied it down the right against Jordan Thomas when the chance arose.

Later on in the half, alert covering defence denied Jackson a clean connection when well placed after being found by Antoni Sarcevic following an eye-catching backheel close to the byline from Powell.

At the other end, Rovers had a couple of half-decent movements down the sides, but there were relatively few alarms for the home defence.

Going the other way, the onus was on City to do a bit more on the resumption, playing in front of the Kop - and be a touch quicker to pull Rovers out of their shape without the ball. They needed a spark and it would arrive on 55 minutes.

Callum Connolly’s juicy cross on the right saw Powell get in between a couple of defenders before confidently steering a well-placed header past Tommy Simkin.

The onus was on Rovers to throw a bit more caution to the wind.

Speaking of caution, both McCann and Duff saw incurred the ire of referee Darren Drysdale with emotions following a fracas in the box between Morgan and Broadbent, who had a pop at each other in the box, sparking a kerfuffle between both sets of players.

A low-grade derby was finally getting spiced up.

A brilliant reaction save from Simkin then denied substitute Humphrys after Pennington flicked on Ibou Touray’s right-wing corner before a huge chance at the other end saw Thomas cut inside and fire a low shot inches wide.

Rovers, who made a triple change with James Collins on for his debut alongside Alfie May and Leon Ayinde, started to up it.

Thomas knocked on wood with a first-time volley from Broadbent’s corner before persistence paid off for the winger, firing home splendidly after Collins knock-down.

Rovers' joy was short-lived with replacement Will Swan spotting Humphrys in space and his drilled finish was inch-perfect.

Simkin was then forced into more work to turn away Humphrys’ fierce drive. But Grehan had the final word.
