#1924. Hull City vs. Brighton & Hove Albion - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:07

Brighton & Hove Albion travel to the MKM Stadium to face Hull City in Sunday's gameweek 11 contest, marking the teams' first-ever Premier League meeting.

The top flight's leading scorers occupy unfamiliar territory in second place, five points behind Arsenal, and Fabian Hurzeler's men are favourites to beat a Hull side without a victory in any competition since late August.

Had Sergej Jakirovic been offered 13th place after 10 matches before the season began, he might have accepted it, given that the Tigers had spent nine years away from top-flight football.

Indeed, the promoted outfit's manager may be relieved by his team's current position, considering that last season's Championship playoff winners have not collected maximum points in nearly three months.

An opening pair of victories over Manchester United (2-0) and Coventry City (1-0) gave supporters plenty to celebrate, before the Tigers secured a creditable third consecutive clean sheet by holding Aston Villa to a goalless draw.

Since then, Hull have exited the EFL Cup and failed to win another seven top-flight matches, extending their winless sequence to eight in the league and nine across all competitions while leaving them three points clear of the relegation places.

Jakirovic can take consolation from his team's battling qualities, which have kept all their defeats narrow: they lost 2-1 to Newcastle United, 1-0 at Fulham and 1-0 at Arsenal before the international break.

Notably, the Tigers are one of four teams yet to lose at home in 2026-27, although their seven points from an available 15 fall short of the returns collected by Arsenal (15), Brighton (13) and Leeds (nine).

Hurzeler's men will be mindful of their hosts' stubbornness in front of their supporters and overall competitiveness as the second-placed side seek to extend their unbeaten run on Sunday.

The Seagulls have won three consecutive matches without conceding, including two top-flight victories that have lifted them to second in the Premier League table.

Unlike in previous seasons, Brighton's success has been built on combining their attacking fluency with defensive solidity, highlighted by six clean sheets across their last seven league matches.

The only league fixture in that sequence without a shutout was a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool, but they have since responded by beating Manchester City 1-0 at the Etihad Stadium and overcoming Brentford 2-0 at the Amex.

Having already recorded at least three consecutive top-flight victories twice in 2026, from March to April and September to October, with the latter sequence extending to four wins, Hurzeler's men now seek to achieve the feat for a third time this calendar year.

With no side collecting more points across the last six rounds, Brighton's return of 15 from 18 matching Arsenal's, the travelling supporters will back their team to triumph in this first Premier League meeting with the Tigers.

Brighton & Hove Albion Premier League form:

Brighton & Hove Albion form (all competitions):

Mohamed Belloumi (thigh), Nobel Mendy (knee) and Charlie Hughes (groin) are doubtful for Hull this weekend, while Matt Targett (ankle), Hidemasa Morita (muscle), Eliot Matazo (knee) and Ilyas Ansah (back) are also carrying injuries.

Matt Crooks, though, is back in contention after serving a one-match suspension against Arsenal before the break for accumulating yellow cards.

Belloumi leads Hull's scoring charts with three goals and their overall attacking returns with five direct involvements, underlining the importance of his potential recovery for Sunday; Oli McBurnie, meanwhile, has contributed two goals and as many assists to offer Jakirovic another potential match-winner.

Pascal Gross has been Brighton's standout attacking contributor, with the Germany international registering four goals and as many assists for eight direct involvements this term.

#1922. Chelsea 1-4 Leeds: Dismal Blues roundly beaten as scrutiny on Xabi Alonso grows

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 to record their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.

Daniel Farke’s team conceded six here earlier this season. That wild defeat in the Carabao Cup in September came at a time when Chelsea were playing cavalier football that made a 6-3 scoreline seem normal, but they stand now on the brink watching their season fall apart.

This was not what their supporters were sold when Xabi Alonso was appointed amidst broad smiles six months ago.

The leadership spoke then of lessons having been learned and of a corner turned. What must co-owner Behdad Eghbali and his four-strong team of sporting directors have made of Leeds running rings around their team on their own pitch, cantering to an easy victory with minimal resistance?

They began well here, 23-year-old striker Emmanuel Emegha firing them ahead early on his full debut, but within minutes they had gifted Okafor an equaliser, a lovely finish into the corner facilitated by static Chelsea defending.

Morgan Rogers might have been unfortunate to concede the penalty at the start of the second half, which was converted by the excellent Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but that decision was not the reason Chelsea were beaten so soundly.

Chelsea player ratings vs Leeds: Palmer anonymous as Blues humiliated

Chelsea handed fresh injury blow as Caicedo forced off against Leeds

Who is Olutayo Subuloye? Chelsea youngster on bench for Leeds clash

Okafor quickly made it three for Leeds, Branden Aronson got a fourth in stoppage time, as Chelsea slumped into mid-table.

Leeds were quickly on the front foot and might have lead early. A wonderful cross from James Justin was met by Calvert-Lewin, ghosting between two defenders to head against the crossbar.

Moises Caicedo was forced off after 20 minutes after a landing awkwardly, arguably the point at which the hosts began to lose their way. Calvert-Lewin soon found room again amongst Chelsea’s defence for a header that was this time straight at Emiliano Martinez.

Emegha’s goal was Chelsea’s only bright spot. Justin made a mess of a clearing header and gave it to Rogers, who nipped past Nico Elvedi and slipped it left for Emegha to take a touch and finish like a striker that had been crashing them in at the Shed End for years.

The manner in which Chelsea let Leeds back level two minutes later will have infuriated Alonso. Josh Acheampong misjudged the bounce of the ball in midfield and Calvert-Lewin stole in and fed Okafor.

There were then three defenders in blue standing motionless around Okafor inside the box as he took aim and rolled the ball into the corner of Martinez’s goal.

A wonderful Calvert-Lewin back-flick was inches from putting Leeds ahead. A goal then would have not unfairly reflected the balance of the first half. Chelsea were a mess and were booed off at the break.

It took an age for VAR to determine that Michael Oliver had been correct to call handball against Rogers from Jayden Bogle’s driven effort in the 48th minute. Rogers had motioned towards the ball which cannoned away of a combination of upper arm and shoulder, but Chelsea felt aggrieved. From the spot, Calvert-Lewin sent Martinez the wrong way.

Okafor whacked in his second and Leeds’ third just before the half-hour, a deflected cross sitting up for a lovely half-volley into the top corner.

Now was the time for another two-goal Chelsea fightback as on that bizarre night in September. Predictably, it never materialised, only another goal from Aronson and more boos for Alonso’s players at the end.

#1918. Getafe vs Atletico Madrid - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 13:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 13:03

Atletico Madrid will be aiming to avoid a third straight defeat in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Getafe on Sunday.

This is a fixture that has been played on 47 occasions throughout history, with Atletico comfortably leading the overall head-to-head record 32 victories to Getafe's five.

Getafe have been beaten in five of their last six matches against Atletico, but they do have a recent home win to their name over the Red and Whites, triumphing 2-1 in March 2025.

The Deep Blue Ones have a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them in 15th spot in the La Liga table.

Jose Bordalas' side entered the November international break off the back of a 2-0 defeat to Villarreal, while they were also beaten 1-0 by Brighton & Hove Albion in the Conference League in their last home fixture on November 5.

Getafe have the joint-worst attacking record in Spain's top flight this season, having only managed to find the back of the net on eight occasions in 12 matches.

The Deep Blue Ones are only two points outside of the relegation zone, but they have been impressive on home soil this season, boasting a record of three wins and three draws from their six league fixtures in front of their own supporters.

Atletico, meanwhile, sit third in the La Liga table, boasting a record of nine wins, one draw and two defeats from their 12 matches to collect 28 points.

Diego Simeone's side are two points behind second-placed Real Madrid and five points off the leaders Barcelona, who beat the Red and Whites 2-1 before the November international break.

Atletico also lost to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on November 3, so they will be bidding to avoid a third straight loss in all competitions in this fixture.

The Red and Whites have been impressive on their travels in Spain's top flight this season, picking up 15 points from their six league games on the road.

Atletico will be bidding to record their 10th league victory of the season on Sunday before welcoming Viking to Madrid in their next Champions League match on November 25.

Getafe will be without the services of Nemenja Gudelj, who is suspended after picking up a milestone yellow card in the clash with Villarreal last time out.

Christiantus Uche, Zaid Romero and Juanmi will also miss out through injury.

Enes Unal is the capital outfit's leading goalscorer this season with four, and there should be another start in the final third of the field for the 29-year-old.

As for Atletico, Alejandro Grimaldo needs to be assessed due to a recent illness, while Marc Pubill is a doubt due to an injury that he sustained on international duty with Spain.

Ademola Lookman and Cristian Romero are also expected to miss out this weekend.

Morten Hjulmand could return in the middle of the Atletico midfield, while Julian Alvarez is likely to be joined in the final third of the field by Lee Kang-in.

Soria; Carvajal, Boselli, Djene, Mojica; Garcia, Terrats, Mangala, Martin; Unal, Satriano

Atletico Madrid possible starting lineup:

Oblak; Llorente, Le Normand, Hancko, Grimaldo; Simeone, Hjulmand, Barrios, Baena; Lee, Alvarez

Getafe have found it difficult to score this season, so we are backing Atletico to keep a clean sheet in a much-needed victory on Sunday.

#1917. Coventry 3-2 Crystal Palace: Eagles stay bottom as Sky Blues edge thriller to spoil Thomas Frank’s debut

Thomas Frank suffered defeat in his first game as Crystal Palace boss as Dwight McNeil’s late own goal condemned them to a 3-2 loss at Coventry.

Frank, who was sacked by Tottenham in February, oversaw his first game for a third London club but was unable to stop them from losing for a fifth successive match in the Premier League.

Frank’s tenure got off to the worst start possible when Taiwo Awoniyi put the hosts in front with his second goal of the campaign, but Palace instantly responded through Yeremy Pino.

An all-action first half continued as Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s sublime strike put Coventry back in front before Jorgen Strand Larsen’s first goal since September pulled Palace level again.

It looked like Palace would come away with a point until McNeil inadvertently bundled the ball into his own net to secure Coventry back-to-back home wins.

Frank Lampard’s side are growing in confidence in front of their own supporters and picked up a third win at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

What Frank must change at Crystal Palace if new era is to succeed

Lampard was wary of the visitors starting strongly with a new boss, but it was his side who drew first blood when Jack Rudoni played the ball across for Awoniyi to stab a first-time effort into the far corner.

The hosts were left wondering how they were not two to the good when, seconds after Carl Rushworth’s save down one end, the Sky Blues broke through Awoniyi and he rounded Dean Henderson but saw his effort blocked heroically by Axel Disasi on the goal-line.

They were made to pay shortly afterwards as Palace levelled.

Daichi Kamada sent a cross in towards Strand Larsen who saw his failed scorpion attempt bounce kindly for Pino and he lashed home from close range.

Coventry regained their advantage on the half-hour mark courtesy of a sublime hit by Sakamoto.

Rudoni had assisted the first and was the creator again as he whipped a cross to Sakamoto who took a lovely touch with his chest before lashing a shot past Henderson from outside the box.

Palace came from behind for a second time on the stroke of half-time. Pino turned creator with a cross onto the head of Strand Larsen, who had sprung the offside the trap and nodded the ball beyond Rushworth.

Henderson was called into action to stop Coventry from going ahead for a third time as he dived to his right to palm Rudoni’s effort behind.

Palace were in the ascendancy and looking most likely to get their noses in front.

Strand Larsen was first onto a low cross by Pino but he was stopped by Rushworth and Bobby Thomas made a crucial block to stop substitute Evann Guessand from sweeping the ball home.

It proved vital as Coventry snatched a winner. Brandon Thomas-Asante’s initial header was saved by Henderson but the ball bounced off McNeil and rolled over the line.

#1915. Man Utd chief Omar Berrada breaks silence on Man City charges and denies involvement

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved ‘in any wrongdoings’ during his time at Manchester City amid the ongoing case against his former employers.

An independent commission found City guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League’s financial rules in September between the period of 2009 and 2018.

City have appealed against the ruling and repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

Berrada joined United in January 2024 having spent over a decade working in various roles for City Football Group.

He was named the club’s CEO in 2016 and remained in that role until 2020 when he was named City Football Group’s chief football operations officer for the next four years.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Berrada’s time at the club’s CEO overlaps with the period in which City were investigated. But the United chief has no concerns over any implications for him in the case.

‘I’m not concerned,’ Berrada told Sky Sports.

‘I want to be very clear about this: I wasn’t involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn’t involved in the proceedings. There are no allegations against me.

‘In that sense, there will be no surprises.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Asked whether United could look to pursue compensation if City fail in their appeal, Berrada replied: ‘I don’t want to comment on that because right now, it’s an ongoing process.

‘When it runs its course, then we’ll take a view on what is our position as Manchester United.’

Berrada and the rest of United’s hierarchy have just presided over their third mid-season managerial sacking in three years with Mauricio Pochettino the latest to be tasked with lifting the club from its malaise.

‘If you think about the fact that we’ve had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven’t achieved the stability that we want to – that’s for sure,’ Berrada said.

‘There are different circumstances as to why it didn’t work out with Erik, Ruben and now Michael. And we’re always learning. We’re always trying to improve and understand what has failed.’

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 13:32, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 13:34

Malaga's search for their first victory of the 2026-27 La Liga campaign will continue on Sunday, when they head to Estadio El Sadar to tackle Osasuna.

The White and Sky Blues are the only team in Spain's top flight yet to triumph this term, and they are in danger of becoming cut adrift at the bottom of the La Liga table.

Osasuna boast a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them in 16th spot in the division.

Jagoba Arrasate's side entered the November international break off the back of a 1-1 draw with Athletic Bilbao, but they did start the month with a 2-1 loss to Deportivo La Coruna.

The Little Reds finished 17th in Spain's top flight last season, level on points with 18th-placed Mallorca, only surviving on head-to-head points.

As a result, there is plenty of room for improvement during the current campaign, but consistency has been a problem in the opening months of the season.

Osasuna have only won seven of their previous 32 matches against Malaga in all competitions, suffering 12 defeats in the process, while there have also been 13 draws.

Malaga are winless in their last four games against Osasuna, though, and they have beaten Sunday's opponents just once since April 2013.

This match will mark the first fixture between the two teams since March 2019, when Osasuna recorded a 2-1 victory, while they also won 2-1 in the reverse game in the same season.

Malaga are rock bottom of the La Liga table, only picking up five points from their opening 12 matches of the season, boasting a record of zero wins, five draws and seven defeats.

Juan Francisco Funes' side entered the November international break off the back of successive defeats to Real Betis and Racing de Santander.

Los Albicelestes also have the joint-second worst defensive record in La Liga this season with 23 goals conceded, while they have the second-worst attack with only nine goals scored.

Osasuna need to make late checks on Aimar Oroz, Jorge Herrando and Romain Del Castillo before final decisions on the trio can be made.

There are not expected to be any surprises in the Osasuna XI for this match, with Ante Budimir again set to lead the line; the experienced striker has eight goals in 12 appearances this term.

Ruben Garcia and Raul Moro are also expected to feature in the final third of the field, while there should be a spot in the middle of the midfield for Lucas Torro.

As for Malaga, Adam Aznou is suspended following his red card against Racing last time out.

Juan Cruz, Julen Lobete, Diego Murillo, Aaron Ochoa and Carlos Puga are also expected to be absent for the away side due to injury problems.

Adrian Nino has scored five times in eight appearances this season, and the 22-year-old will again feature in the final third of the field for the White and Sky Blues.

#1912. Omar Berrada hits back at criticism over Manchester United’s transfer strategy

Manchester United’s CEO Omar Berrada has hit back at criticism of the club’s transfer strategy last summer and insists a ‘disciplined’ approach is required.

United spent £155 million on signing three midfielders in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba in the summer transfer window.

However, Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford this week without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is out for the remainder of the year with a shin problem, while Luke Shaw has missed United’s last seven games due to injury.

United supporters have criticised the club’s decision to only strengthen Michael Carrick’s midfield in the summer but Berrada is adamant the squad is ‘fundamentally better’ after their signings.

‘You have to take it in the context of the last few years,’ Berrada told Sky Sports.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The summer of 2025, I think the recruitment team was widely praised with the four players that were signed. And they did very well. They helped the team achieve Champions League qualification.

‘When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It’s probably been the summer or the transfer window where there’s been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

‘And we’ve said publicly and we’ve said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs.

‘And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we’re receiving a lot of criticism for it but we’re actually happy with the players that we bought.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, and let’s not forget that we’ve also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona – these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

‘It’s true that we lost Casemiro, who is a top player and gave a lot to the club. We also lost Manuel Ugarte to, unfortunately, an ACL injury. So our focus was very much about straightening the midfield.

‘When we started the transfer window, we really only had Kobbie Mainoo as our midfielder. So we wanted to reinforce that, and we did it.’

Berrada also addressed United’s decision not to sign a new left-sided defender after the club made an enquiry for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

‘When you look at the other areas of the pitch, and there’s a lot of discussion about the back line,’ Berrada said.

‘But we did come into it thinking we have depth. We have nine players that can play in the back line, in the back four positions.

‘So that’s why we looked primarily at investing in the midfield. But we were always looking for opportunities. I think it’s been widely reported that we were looking at potentially the left-back position as a reinforcement.

‘I think what we’ve seen in the back line is we’ve had injuries, it’s taken Matthijs de Ligt longer than we would want it to get back. Unfortunately, Luke Shaw suffered a muscle injury that meant he was out for five or six weeks.

‘So could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players and you have to find the right players at the right value.

‘There’s no point in us spending £40 million, £50m for players that we’re not convinced are going to add value to the team.

‘So it’s always about being disciplined and finding the right opportunities and getting the right players that are going to take us forward.

‘When I talk about being disciplined, I talk about not overspending on players that don’t necessarily add quality to the team.

‘Because when you sign a player that doesn’t work out for Man Utd, it becomes very difficult to move that player on or to get the sale we want. And that can set us back.

‘So when I talk about being disciplined, I’m not talking about necessarily not spending to get the top players. We have the ambition to win, to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups. And for that, we need top talent. So when we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don’t want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it.’

#1911. Thomas Tuchel's 'best night' as England manager: Three Lions boss hails heroes after Spain victory - but hits out at Elliot Anderson decision made by referee he previously labelled a 'one out of 10'

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss

'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'

#1907. Hull City vs. Brighton: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 13:39

Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion travel to face Hull City on Sunday as Fabian Hurzeler's side look to extend their impressive run of form in the clubs' first-ever Premier League meeting.

Sergej Jakirovic's Tigers sit 13th after 10 matches and three points clear of the relegation zone, having gone eight league games without a victory despite remaining unbeaten on home soil this season.

Conversely, the Seagulls arrive full of confidence after recording consecutive top-flight wins over Manchester City and Brentford, boasting six clean sheets across their last seven league outings.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Hull and Brighton.

Nearly 67 years have passed since Hull City and Brighton & Hove Albion first locked horns - a November 1959 Division Two clash that ended in a 3-1 victory for the Tigers - and there have now been 51 competitive meetings between the two clubs in all competitions.

The Seagulls hold the bragging rights when it comes to overall victories with 22, while Hull have claimed 15 wins of their own and another 14 contests have seen the spoils shared.

Remarkably, none of those 51 encounters have taken place in the Premier League, with every previous battle arriving in the Football League or the FA Cup, and the two sides have not crossed paths since a goalless Championship stalemate in East Yorkshire in February 2016.

Recent clashes between the pair have been notably tight, low-scoring affairs, with none of their last nine meetings across all competitions settled by more than a single goal and three ending 0-0.

During the 2015-16 campaign, both clubs collected a narrow 1-0 victory on home soil - Brighton prevailing in the Championship in September 2015 before Hull gained revenge in the FA Cup four months later - prior to that goalless draw in February.

Indeed, home advantage has heavily dictated this fixture in the modern era, as Hull are unbeaten in their last six home games against Brighton across all competitions - winning four and keeping five clean sheets - since suffering a 2-0 Division Three defeat in October 2000.

Conversely, the Tigers have endured a miserable record on the South Coast, failing to win any of their last 22 visits to Brighton since recording their sole away triumph in this fixture - a 2-1 Division Three success - way back in August 1965.

Brighton built much of their overall head-to-head lead during a dominant spell in the late 1980s and 1990s, rattling off four straight victories between October 1989 and April 1991 before later embarking on a nine-match unbeaten run from April 1993 to December 1996.

That sequence included the Seagulls' biggest-ever win in this matchup, a resounding 4-0 Division Two triumph in March 1996, while they also completed a comfortable league double over Hull with 2-0 and 3-0 victories in the 2000-01 Division Three season.

Hull's most emphatic triumph came in the highest-scoring meeting between the two sides, a 5-2 Division Two victory in December 1988, while they also put three unanswered goals past Brighton in March 1997.

The two teams have also collided five times in the FA Cup, with Brighton winning the first two ties in January 1985 (1-0) and January 1986 (3-2) before Hull turned the tide by edging a 2-1 replay victory in February 2014 following a 1-1 draw and claiming that 1-0 success in January 2016.

#1902. Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea sack prediction could come true as Leeds expose everything wrong with BlueCo project

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso had been clear that he wanted his Chelsea team to match Leeds physically and mentally in the spirit of this historically feisty fixture.

What he got in the end, though, was yet more evidence that this young team are there for the taking by those who want to take the game to them.

Leeds were sharper and nastier in every aspect today, and while Chelsea took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha, it came as no surprise to see Daniel Farke’s men snap back to equalise before running away with the game with such ferocity that Alonso’s future will, for the first time, come under some scrutiny.

There were boos at the break with the score level, but Leeds firmly on top, and the shower of condemnation that followed the full-time whistle vocalised in the clearest terms that Alonso is under pressure.

Alonso’s Blues started the season ferociously and looked like they could challenge for major honours, but Chelsea supporters have been here before.

They were always going to need more than a few exhilarating attacking displays to nail their names to the mast of a title challenge, and so it has proved.

Chelsea player ratings vs Leeds: Four 3/10s as Palmer anonymous

Dismal Chelsea well beaten by Leeds as scrutiny on Alonso grows

Chelsea handed fresh injury blow as Caicedo forced off against Leeds

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

Chelsea are nowhere near runaway leaders Arsenal, and they are once again looking over their shoulders at sides who are less well-resourced but more tactically defined and mentally resolute.

Leeds dominated both boxes and were first to every ball, bullying Chelsea’s defence just as Sunderland and Brian Brobbey had before the international break.

Lessons have not been learned from last week, from last season or, frankly, any point of the BlueCo ownership. Chelsea as a team, while not short on quality, remain short of leaders.

They have looked to shoehorn young men into positions of responsibility, and this is the inevitable result. Teams with nous, experience and bite will continue to see Stamford Bridge as a challenge they can scale.

This was Leeds’ first win in this corner of west London since the turn of the millennium, the latest in a long list of teams to head to a formerly impenetrable Stamford Bridge and make history.

Chelsea rarely have answers for teams who seek to raise the temperature of the game. When the game becomes stretched, Chelsea become increasingly erratic and tempestuous.

It is in these moments that the typically composed Alonso must do more to change the tide. His changes this afternoon came too late and made no difference. Leeds were in control of the game and the scoreline when Alonso turned to his bench just past the hour mark.

During his introductory press conference over the summer, Alonso was reluctant to say he believed he would get time to instil his ideas. His pessimism appears well placed because, just 11 games into the season, the pressure is ramping up.

#1901. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners 'join' Real Madrid in race for Bayern Munich attacker

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 13:41, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:10

Arsenal have reportedly joined Real Madrid in the race to sign Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise.

The 24-year-old joined Bayern in the summer of 2024 from Crystal Palace and has established himself as one of the finest wingers in European football.

The Frenchman has scored 54 goals and provided 61 assists in 122 appearances, although even those phenomenal numbers do not fully reflect what he brings to the Bayern side.

During the summer transfer window, Real Madrid were heavily linked with a move for Olise, but Bayern made it clear that the winger was not for sale at any price.

Bayern have reportedly placed a £265m valuation on Olise, who is under contract at the Allianz Arena until 2029.

However, club CEO Herbert Hainer has made it clear that no such asking price has been set for the player, whom they want to keep for many years to come.

According to Christian Falk, Arsenal are among the clubs interested in Olise, although it could prove difficult for the Gunners to prise him away from Bayern.

If Olise does decide to leave Munich, a move to La Liga could make more sense, having already experienced life in the Premier League.

There is also a significant gap between Olise's earnings and those of Harry Kane at Bayern, and the German club are expected to do everything in their power to convince the winger to sign a new contract.

The Bild journalist said: "Every club has Michael Olise on their shortlist. There’s a lot of respect for Arsenal, but there are some really big players at the table, like Real Madrid.

"Olise has already played in the Premier League, so I strongly suspect a move to La Liga would be the next logical step were he to look for a move away from Munich.

"That all said, Bayern Munich have proven that big personal awards like the Ballon d’Or can still be won at FC Bayern. So, that’s the hope of the club and they’ll do everything in their power to keep Olise at the Allianz Arena."

Olise could still be tempted to stay at Bayern after seeing his club teammate Harry Kane win the Ballon d'Or this year.

A move to a more competitive league could appeal to the Frenchman, while he may also want to join a club where his chances of winning the Champions League are high.

Bayern have not set an asking price for Olise and could demand a staggering fee, with paying such an amount likely to be nothing short of madness.

Arsenal arguably need a right winger who can provide reliable cover for Bukayo Saka rather than a player of Olise's calibre, who would expect to be a guaranteed starter if he made the move to the Emirates Stadium.

#1900. Hutchinson admits ‘dream’ is to be bought by Milan and insists Scudetto is possible

Omari Hutchinson has spoken about his preferred role, while praising the AC Milan fans and revealing his belief the Scudetto is a realistic target.

Hutchinson joined Milan on an initial loan deal from Nottingham Forest with an option to buy. He scored his first goal for the club in the away win over Udinese last month, and is getting more regular minutes on the right side.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, the head coach Ruben Amorim has even deployed him as a wing-back on occasion. Given the injuries to Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze the Englishman’s role has become an even more important one than first imagined.

Hutchinson met with fans this afternoon at the Milan Store in San Babila in the city centre. While at the event, the winger gave an interview to the reporters who were present, with MilanNews relaying his words.

How have these first few months at Milan been? Are you raising your game?

“It’s going well, the coach is happy, but I think there’s still a lot to do. I’m earning myself some space… From here on out, we have to keep winning.”

We often see you on the wing. Do you prefer to play there or as a second striker?

“Personally, I like to play anywhere, but preferably on the right flank. Then, wherever the coach puts me, I try to adapt, do my job, and perform to my best, following his tactical instructions. He knows what I can do with the ball. He simply tells me to create and give my all.”

“He talks to me about what to do with the ball and to do my best.”

Why this difference in performance between Serie A and the Europa League?

“It’s hard to say… There have been games where we haven’t performed well due to silly mistakes, but I think we need to push forward from now on and get back on track for the Europa League. We have the right team to do it. We need to win and be at our best in every game.”

What has struck you most about the fans in Italy these past months?

“Definitely the passion surrounding the club. At the stadium, everyone is behind the team. It’s fantastic, I’ve never experienced anything like it before.”

“We’ve got the players, we have a good squad, and even though we’re still missing some leaders at times, I think we’re building on that. I think the coaches and the coaching staff are guiding us very well. Once everything clicks together perfectly, we’ll do great things.”

Do you still see yourself at Milan in the coming seasons?

“It’s my dream. After this season, I hope to be signed permanently. I see myself playing here for a long time to come.”

What’s the feeling of playing in a historic stadium like San Siro?

“It’s crazy. The fans, even the away fans… It’s a unique feeling. It makes you want to give your all for the fans, create special moments, and win.”

What are the differences between the Premier League and Serie A?

“They’re both tough. When other teams play against Milan, they always want to give their all. They’re always tough matches. Tactically, it’s more defensive here.

“In the Premier League, you probably have more space and the quality is probably a little higher, but Serie A is a tough league. There’s not that big a difference, there’s not that big a gap.”

Is there any team-mate you’ve grown close to?

“No, I have a good relationship with everyone. They’ve all welcomed me very well, and obviously it’s easier with the guys who speak English.”

Do you dream of making the national team?

“I’m trying to focus on my club. I want to perform well for Milan and then we’ll see.”

#1897. Xabi Alonso delivers Moises Caicedo injury update as Chelsea star hit with fresh setback

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso says Chelsea will not know the severity of Moises Caicedo’s injury until later this week.

The Ecuador international went down off the ball just past the 20-minute mark of Chelsea’s grim loss to Leeds on Saturday, and received treatment before being replaced by Jordan Henderson.

Caicedo has struggled for fitness all season and asked to be substituted at half-time during Ecuador’s 2-0 friendly win over Bolivia this week while on international duty.

The 25-year-old was deemed fit enough to start against Leeds, but was on the end of a number of heavy challenges early on at Stamford Bridge, including an incident which saw him require treatment after landing awkwardly on his back.

Speaking at full-time, Alonso delivered an update on his condition, saying: “Xabi Alonso delivers Moises Caicedo injury update as Chelsea star hit with fresh setback.”

The match was goalless when Caicedo was withdrawn, but Chelsea soon took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha before being quickly pegged back by Noah Okafor’s leveller.

It quickly unravelled after the break, though, as Noah Okafor’s brace and Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s penalty put the Blues to the sword.

“It went wrong after the equaliser, after the change (with) Moi, we completely lost the momentum,” Alonso mused. “Until then, we were doing okay, I think that we were creating, playing a lot on the pitch, we were coming out of the pressure.

Chelsea are already managing several injuries to key players, with Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix and Reece James all sidelined.

Alonso is also expected to provide an update on Caicedo in his post-match press conference later this afternoon.

#1896. Cole Palmer in angry exchange with injured Chelsea teammate after Leeds defeat

Xabi Alonso’s side were thrashed 4-1 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon with the visitors scoring three times in the second-half to seal a famous win in the capital.

Emmanuel Emegha opened the scoring for the hosts after 25 minutes before Noah Okafor levelled the contest three minutes later.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin put Leeds back in front eight minutes into the second-half before Okafor added his second of the afternoon.

Glenn Murray believes Bruno Fernandes will look to leave the club if he doesn’t sign a new Manchester United contract before the January transfer window.

Fernandes won the PFA Players’ Player of the Year last year after a superb second half of the season under Michael Carrick, but has not hit those same heights so far this campaign.

The Red Devils captain was also dropped for a game after publicly criticising Carrick’s tactics following a heavy Champions League defeat to Como.

The arrival of Mauricio Pochettino represents a fresh start for Fernandes this season, but there remains uncertainty over his long-term future at the club given the 32-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season.

Fernandes has already turned down two contract offers from the club, and former Brighton striker Murray believes he could be eyeing up a move away from Old Trafford when the transfer window reopens in January.

‘I think if he gets the option to move on, and it gets to January, and he can start speaking to other people, I think it will open his eyes up to see where he could go and if he could win things and finish off his career more enjoyably, because there have been years at Manchester United that have been really difficult.

#1890. Grief-stricken Tenerife stars return to action for first time since death of Jesus de Miguel, 30, after fatal on-field collision with goalkeeper: Tributes paid and match paused in 9th minute on emotional day

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso believes that Leeds would not have been awarded a penalty in their 4-1 thrashing of Chelsea had referee Michael Oliver not given the decision on the field.

Leeds came from behind to secure their first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999, heaping pressure on Alonso as Chelsea lost for the third time in four Premier League games.

The hosts took the lead in the 25th minute through Emmanuel Emegha but were quickly pegged back when Noah Okafor squeezed his shot into the far corner three minutes later.

Leeds took the lead early in the second-half after they were awarded a contentious penalty when Morgan Rogers was adjudged to have handled Jayden Bogle’s attempt at goal.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored the resulting spot-kick, which was awarded after a VAR review, and from there Leeds ran away with the game scoring through Okafor and Brenden Aaronson.

Calvert-Lewin’s penalty was a turning point in the game despite Leeds’ dominance, and asked about the decision Alonso said he did not believe the referee and the VAR made the right decision. “No, I don’t agree, I don’t agree,” Alonso said in his post-match press conference.

#1887. Report: Six clubs interested in Milan midfielder Jashari including four domestic rivals

A number of clubs are interested in signing Ardon Jashari from AC Milan, according to a report from his native Switzerland.

Jashari has once again found himself playing largely as a back-up under Ruben Amorim this season, after performing the role of being Luka Modric’s deputy during his debut campaign with the Rossoneri under Massimiliano Allegri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Given that over €30m was invested to sign him from Club Brugge, a bigger role and impact was perhaps foreseen by all parties. Thus, Jashari’s situation is one to monitor, and there is certainly no shortage of interested parties.

According to information from 4-4-2.ch, clubs in both Serie A and the Premier League are seriously considering a move for the 24-year-old midfielder, who started last night in Switzerland’s 4-0 win over Scotland and impressed.

Roma, Juventus, Atalanta and Como are the four Italian clubs that are looking at the Swiss international. From England, it is Aston Villa and Nottingham Forest that are monitoring his situation closely.

Jashari is under contract until 2030, so Milan have leverage, and they have not yet received a concrete offer. However, this could change as January gets closer. The Rossoneri still highly value Jashari, even though he hasn’t yet established himself as a regular starter.

A permanent sale would therefore require a fee in the range of €35-40m. Milan paid Club Brugge a similar sum for him a year ago and they have no intention of making a loss, given his age and potential.

#1886. Liverpool vs. Man Utd: Andoni Iraola confirms quadruple injury boost in major team news update

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 14:06

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has confirmed a quadruple injury boost for his side ahead of Sunday's blockbuster Premier League battle with Manchester United at Anfield.

The Reds have the honour of hosting Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the Red Devils, in which they will endeavour to improve on a paltry record of just one win from five home matches in the 2026-27 top flight.

Liverpool maintained their excellent away form by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 before the international break, but Dominik Szoboszlai emerged as an injury worry following the Selhurst Park success.

The midfielder nevertheless joined up with Hungary for the November international break and played the full 90 in both of their Nations League games against Georgia and Northern Ireland, supplying two assists against the former.

Szoboszlai was managing a knee problem during his time with the Magyars, but speaking to the media on Friday, Iraola affirmed that the 26-year-old will be fine for Sunday's main event.

"He's in a good place, he's playing normally, he was not even strapped today so he's fine yes," Iraola responded when asked if Szoboszlai was still being carefully looked after.

As well as confirming Szoboszlai's availability, Iraola delivered positive updates on the Dutch trio of Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong and Virgil van Dijk.

The latter withdrew from the Netherlands squad for the November window due to an unspecified fitness problem, while Gravenberch and Frimpong were both absent from the win over Palace.

Frimpong sustained a hamstring injury against Brentford in October and has missed Liverpool's last six games in all competitions, while Gravenberch has been dealing with a minor heal fracture.

However, all three are in line to feature against old rivals Man United, as Iraola added: "If everything goes to plan they should be available for the game.

"Gravenberch, it's a matter of pain, he's managing but he's been training the last two days. Jeremie is recovering the same. We've introduced him with the rest of the group, and Virgil is fine to go."

Should all of Szoboszlai, Van Dijk, Gravenberch and Frimpong make the cut, Liverpool's only remaining concerns are the long-term trio of Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitike.

The latter is still a while away from making a full recovery from an Achilles injury, but Leoni and Bradley have returned to team training as they close in on returns from serious knee injuries.

However, Iraola confirmed that neither defender will be in the squad on Sunday, adding: "The international break was the best moment to introduce them slowly, they've started doing things with the team. They are still not available, but it's very good news and I hope they can play in some weeks."

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points from their opening 10 games, but they have won just two of their last nine matches against Man Utd.

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 14:08

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has revealed that Joao Pedro remains unavailable for Saturday's Premier League fixture against Leeds United.

However, despite suggesting that he was dealing with fitness issues while on international duty with Ecuador, Moises Caicedo has been declared fit.

The Blues return to action this weekend sitting in fifth place in the Premier League table, yet Alonso is under pressure to deliver after four defeats in 10 top-flight matches.

Pedro has been sidelined since the October 17 game at Everton with a thigh injury, and it remains unclear when he will return.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Alonso stated that two players had been passed fit, while three players in total are still ruled out.

When quizzed on Pedro, the Spaniard told reporters: "Not yet. He's not fit yet to train with the team.

"He's not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling."

Alonso went on to say that Maxence Lacroix, who suffered a hamstring injury versus Liverpool on October 28, was in a similar situation to Pedro, while Jorrel Hato remains out with a back problem.

Nevertheless, as well as Caicedo being passed fit, Josh Acheampong will be back in the squad after missing one Premier League game and two England Under-21 matches with a minor issue.

Meanwhile, Alonso has added that Reece James is still "some weeks away" from returning from a knee injury that required surgery.

However, despite not being back in contention this week, Alonso revealed that Jamie Gittens is training with the first-team squad after six weeks out with an ankle injury.

#1880. More than just a football club: Cardinale’s vision to make AC Milan a multi-billion empire

In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has big plans for AC Milan.

The RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment. Of course AC Milan will be at the centre of the web, but the idea is to expand.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The proof of this comes from a three-letter acronym: MSE. It stands for Milan Sports & Entertainment and it is the new holding company created by RedBird. The idea, simply put, is to bring together investments and activities in various sectors under one umbrella.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport recall, Cardinale explained to the Financial Times that the assets involved could be valued in the mid-single-digit billions, meaning several billion dollars. So, how does he plan to get there?

Cardinale linked the creation of MSE to the process initiated with the acquisition of Milan: “Milan Sports & Entertainment is the culmination of this work and of what we have built since we first invested in the club four years ago.”

In his interview with La Gazzetta, Cardinale clarified that the new structure is also created to support the Rossoneri’s sporting ambitions: “The driving force behind operations like this is to provide Milan with the financial strength needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.”

There are examples of this kind of model working already. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, AEG and Fenway Sports Group are among the most prominent and – given his background in the USA – Cardinale knows each of them well.

According to CNBC valuations, KSE was worth $26.05bn in 2026, FSG $15.37bn, and AEG $11.99bn in 2025, excluding music and hotel businesses.

KSE boasts franchises such as the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche and Arsenal, as well as venues such as SoFi Stadium, Ball Arena, and Emirates Stadium. The group combines sports, infrastructure and real estate development such as Hollywood Park, the district built around SoFi Stadium.

AEG – founded by Philip Anschutz – have instead built its model on the management and development of venues. It owns or manages venues such as Crypto.com Arena and The O2 in London plus the Los Angeles Kings and LA Galaxy, and operates in concert promotion and ticketing. The LA LIVE project developed around Crypto.com Arena puts the venue at the centre of a greater ecosystem.

Fenway Sports Group – born around the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool FC – have developed a holding company with interests in media, marketing, real estate, and entertainment. It’s a model Cardinale knows first hand: in 2021, RedBird invested approximately $750m in FSG, acquiring a stake of around 11%, based on an enterprise valuation of $7.35bn.

MSE in theory can harness elements of all three of these experiences: KSE’s integration of sports and infrastructure, AEG ‘s commercial development of facilities and FSG ‘s multi-sport approach. The main difference is the purpose declared by Cardinale: to use all of it to funnel money back into Milan.

From the stadium shared with Inter to the possibility of an arena in San Donato, including the new NBA Europe venture and even tennis: MSE’s scope includes various initiatives that go beyond the playing field.

The main infrastructure project is the future Generali Stadium, the new 71,500-seat facility designed by Foster + Partners and Manica. Developed jointly by the two Milanese clubs, it represents a key element of the transformation of the San Siro area and will not be a Rossoneri-only facility.

The promoters intend for the stadium to host year-round activities, from matches to concerts, as well as catering, events, and hospitality services. In other words, like the stadiums and arenas mentioned above, it will become more than just a place to go for two hours on a Sunday.

In San Donato Milanese, RedBird are also considering the possibility of building a 20,000-seat arena. Cardinale explained that the fund already owns the land and has planning permission, but the idea is also linked to Milan’s potential involvement in NBA Europe. Another area of ​​focus concerns tennis, with the possibility of hosting a tournament in the city.

Finally, RedBird intend to develop a company dedicated to managing stadiums and arenas, with services including catering, merchandising and premium hospitality. The goal is to build commercial expertise to apply to the facilities connected to the group, but also to make it available to other owners and sports clubs.

This phase will be co-ordinated by Brett Yormark, appointed CEO of MSE and set to step down as head of the Big 12 (a conference in College Football) at the end of January 2027. He worked for 14 years at Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment, overseeing the development of the Brooklyn Nets and the Barclays Center. He has also gained experience in NASCAR and Roc Nation.

The choice to go for Yormark reflects the desire to entrust the platform to someone with expertise across multiple different fields in the sporting and commercial worlds.

All these grand plans are well and good, but how will ideas turn into money that drives AC Milan forward? MSE’s economic potential is measured not only through the club’s revenues, but also through the activities that RedBird intends to develop around sports, infrastructure and entertainment.

The starting point is obviously Milan as a club, which closed the 2025-26 financial year with revenues of €464.6m, over €100m of which came from sponsorships. The main infrastructure opportunity is the new San Siro, an investment of approximately €2.3bn shared with Inter.

Projections contained in the design documents indicate a potential annual revenue of approximately €120.4m for the facility as a whole (both for the Rossoneri and the Nerazzurri), through sporting, commercial, and complementary services

These are numbers that will be revised upwards by the two clubs when considering, for example, the record agreement with Generali for naming rights. It is worth a total of €650m over 25 years, divided into €10m per year for the first five years and €30m per season for the following 20, once the stadium is built.

One of the areas on which RedBird Capital are focusing most is hospitality, which is currently worth around €15m per year for the Rossoneri. The international benchmark has already been set by Legends Global, a company Cardinale knows well.

Legends are what the Milan owner sees as a model for developing premium services, restaurants, and commercial spaces. The most obvious example is at FC Barcelona: with the support of LG, the club have marketed nearly 5,000 VIP seats at Camp Nou, generating over €380m in contracted revenue.

They aim to generate another €700m through multi-year licenses for an additional 2,000 seats. This isn’t annual revenue, but rather contracts spread over 15 or 30 years, so a guaranteed flow of money coming in that Cardinale aims to replicate.

Another agreement which demonstrates the potential of this kind of arrangement is the one with Real Madrid for the Santiago Bernabéu. It involves an investment of approximately €360m in exchange for 20-year participation in some of the stadium’s businesses,.

Legends Global also operate in facilities and events management. Following the acquisition of ASM Global (who actually proposed renovating San Siro for non-football events in Italy) in 2024, the group claims a presence in over 450 venues, approximately 20,000 events, and 165 million guests annually. Their European partnerships include Arsenal, Chelsea and Porto.

FC Barcelona launches new VIP seating licenses at Spotify Camp Nou with Legends Global

🔗 More details: https://t.co/awtEsnYE6X pic.twitter.com/iCMuM0QD35

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 25, 2026

To illustrate the potential it could hold for Italy as a whole, the English subsidiary reported revenues of £131.6m in 2024, of which £105.5m came from facility and event management and £26.1m from catering. Before the integration with ASM Global, Legends had reported revenues of $1.7bn in the period ending in March 2024, with 67% coming from food and beverage sales.

In Italy, a benchmark is Forumnet, who in 2024 generated €29.7m in revenue and €12.8m in EBITDA (Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation). They manage the Assago Forum which hosts approximately 60-70 concerts a year, demonstrating how a venue can generate activity well beyond the sports calendar.

As mentioned, an arena is being planned in San Donato with an estimated investment of around €400m, which could become the basis for a Milanese franchise in NBA Europe. For reference, Olimpia Milano – the current basketball team in the city – generate around €15m through ticketing, season tickets, sponsorships and merchandising.

For NBA Europe, projections speak of over $1.5bn to be distributed to the clubs in the first six years. A theoretical division among the 12 permanent franchises would equate to approximately $20.8m per team per year, but this is not fixed yet. Entry costs – estimated by the media to be between $500m and over $1bn – also remain to be determined.

Tennis represents another potential area for development. The ATP 500 in Halle generates around €5m in revenue, excluding television rights, while the ATP Finals in Turin generate around €60m. These are events with different dimensions and scopes, but they provide a scale.

The creation of MSE has a stated objective: to strengthen Milan’s financial capacity and reduce the gap with the richest clubs on the international scene, particularly those in the Premier League.

The gap is also evident when comparing revenues. AC Milan closed the 2025-26 season with €464.6m, a significant result considering their absence from European competitions , but still far from the top English clubs.

According to the Deloitte Football Money League, in the 2024-25 season, Liverpool generated €836.1m, Arsenal €821.7m and Manchester United €793.1m. Tottenham and Chelsea also exceeded €670m and €580m, respectively.

The comparison covers different financial years, but it still shows the magnitude of the gap. Liverpool generated revenues equal to approximately 1.8 times those of Milan, while Chelsea recorded a turnover approximately €120 higher.

The chasm shows how clubs in the Premier League have showcased an ability to generate commercial revenue, enhance stadiums and reach a global audience. The gap has only been growing, and TV rights will be another focus, though that is outside of just Cardinale’s hands.

Speaking of the owner, it is now obvious he sees MSE as the name that will house the tools to try build a real sporting and commercial world around Milan. It remains to be seen how effective it will be, but the starting point is there.

#1879. Ian Wright orders Arsenal to buy £67m star in January following Newcastle draw

Ian Wright has urged Arsenal to go out and buy Antonio Nusa from RB Leipzig in the January transfer window.

Despite a 2-2 draw with Newcastle United on Saturday night, the Gunners remain six points clear at the summit of the Premier League and are still firm favourites to defend their crown.

But their limitations in attack were again exposed on Tyneside. Eberechi Eze opened the scoring on the night with Noni Madueke impressing on the right with Bukayo Saka out injured but the visitors were short on inspiration off the bench.

Christos Tzolis came on in the second-half for a forgettable cameo with Viktor Gyokeres labouring once again after his introduction.

#1878. Mauricio Pochettino swaps one football for another as new Man United boss continues US farewell tour at NFL clash ahead of final game in charge

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 22:54 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 22:55 EST, 15 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.

The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

USMNT and future Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is at the Bengals-Steelers game 😭🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/B7Irn0YLnd

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued at the NFL on Sunday night

The new Manchester United boss attended the Cincinnati Bengals' game at Paycor Stadium

He was greeted by kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow - members of the Bengals' special teams - on the turf before kickoff.

The US is set to face Haiti in the second-leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

The game, which will take place around a mile north of the Bengals' Paycor Stadium, will mark Pochettino's final match in charge of the US national team.

He also took charge of the USA's 6-0 first-leg win against Haiti on Tuesday, which marked the first stop on his farewell tour.

Pochettino will begin his new role with Manchester United on Wednesday, immediately following Tuesday's second-leg. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday.

He emotionally addressed his departure from the US setup and impending new job in a press conference on Friday.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

The Argentine was captured on the sidelines ahead of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

#1877. New Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino "so excited" to be in charge of "amazing club" as Bruno Fernandes update is given

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 14:21

Mauricio Pochettino branded Manchester United "an amazing club" as the Argentine spoke to the media on Friday afternoon at his pre-Liverpool press conference.

Man United sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month before announcing that Pochettino had been appointed as his replacement.

The South American finished his duties with the USA before flying straight to England to begin work on Wednesday, with Man United back in action away to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

Pochettino spoke to reporters at his pre-match press conference on Friday, and he detailed the importance of being ready for the clash with Liverpool.

"We are so excited to be here and I think it's an amazing club. We are happy, but at the same time, so busy. I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool," said Pochettino.

"We arrive with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy with the way we love to work.

"We have found supportive people in the club. But at the same time, we need to improve our players and find a way to perform. The identity and the culture of the club are very clear; it's a historic club with years as one of the best in the world.

"My first target is to sleep! But I cannot sleep, only three or four days a day. The target is to get to know the people, the staff, the players, and try to have an impact from the beginning, a positive one.

"We want to create something different and positive, to build our own way here. We feel the support from day one that we started to work. The most important thing is to think about the next action, not the past."

Pochettino also confirmed that Bruno Fernandes would be remaining as captain of the 20-time English champions amid the speculation surrounding his future.

Fernandes had his issues this season, and it is understood that the Portugal international has rejected the chance to sign a new deal at Old Trafford.

However, Pochettino detailed the importance of the attacker during his press conference, and he is expected to be in the starting XI against Liverpool.

"I think the commitment of all the players is amazing from day one. Bruno is our captain and he's a very important player, but all the player must feel they are important. We chatted yesterday and spent three hours chatting in my office with all the players. I missed some injured players, but in the next few days, I will talk to everyone," he said.

The 32-year-old has scored six goals and registered three assists in 14 appearances for Man United during the 2026-27 campaign.

#1876. Worst-case scenario for Mikel Arteta as Arsenal lose their superpower at Newcastle

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have had worse 45 minutes over the course of Mikel Arteta’s seven years in charge.

However, considering not just the context, but what his players should be capable of, how they let things slip, and what the consequences of one second-half moment in particular might be, this will be right up there as the most frustrating halves he has overseen.

It was all so unnecessary. For years now, a trip up to St James’ Park to take on Newcastle has meant an almighty battle. Brutal, draining encounters, played on the margins and very rarely delivering much joy for the Gunners.

Not here, at least not at first. In the opening 45 minutes, it was the Gunners who were the bullies, bringing an intensity and a level of physicality that Newcastle simply could not live with. By half-time, Arsenal had registered 18 touches in the opposition’s box. Newcastle had managed just one.

Arteta’s side led 1-0 through Eberechi Eze’s emphatic finish but it should have been more. Noni Madueke wasted two big chances. Bruno Guimaraes flung himself at a cross and turned it wide.

There was no reason for this encounter to follow the trend of previous showdowns. It was a Saturday evening stroll for Arsenal and it should have remained as much.

Instead, the Gunners fell apart. Alarmingly so. All it took was one shanked volley from Martin Odegaard, letting Newcastle away on the break to equalise, and the match flipped.

Like in the Champions League win over Slavia Prague last month, Arsenal were dominant in the first half but then let it slip away from them, whether it be complacency or something else. There was no sign of any game management.

Arsenal ratings vs Newcastle: Electric 8/10 star but Bruno Guimaraes run ragged

Arsenal get hammer injury blow as David Raya forced off against Newcastle

In Prague, the opposition did not have the quality to punish them. At St James’ Park, Arsenal paid the price.

From the moment Harvey Barnes equalised, all composure from the visitors evaporated. Madueke swung at thin air attempting to clear. Eze slipped in his own box, Raya could not clear, and Gabriel had to quickly arrive to leather the ball behind.

Arteta looked shell-shocked on the touchline when Newcastle then took the lead from a mess of a corner but the worst was still to come.

David Raya had a collision with William Osula that looked fairly innocuous. When that then forced him off, looking in real pain with an apparent shoulder injury, it felt like a fever dream for Arsenal.

An injury to Raya is the worst-case scenario for the Gunners. There is no player more irreplaceable in this squad.

Arsenal face Manchester City next weekend and then Tottenham a week later. Real Madrid, Manchester United and Bournemouth, who are on a nine-match winning run, all visit north London before Christmas.

The drop-off from Raya to Kepa Arrizabalaga and Illan Meslier is stark. Kepa had his chance in an Arsenal shirt last season and was awful in the Carabao Cup final.

Madueke stepped up to make it 2-2 and ensure Arsenal left Newcastle with a point but there was the sense that the damage had been done.

At half-time, seemingly cruising to another win, Arsenal looked certain to go eight points clear at the top of the table. After City had dropped points to Fulham earlier in the day, there was already a sense that the title race was becoming a one-man show.

Less so now. Not because of a draw with Newcastle, even if a failure to kill off a vulnerable opponent is nothing new for this Arsenal side.

But because without Raya, Arsenal’s defensive strength, the foundations of this team, is far less of a superpower. The severity of that injury might well decide just how much of a title race we have on our hands.

#1875. Man City injury news: Two “doubts” confirmed by Enzo Maresca, Marc Guehi update before Fulham

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 14:21

Enzo Maresca has provided the latest update on the fitness of his Manchester City squad ahead of Saturday lunchtime’s Premier League clash at home to Fulham.

The Citizens enter this contest seeking to end a three-game losing run, with defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion followed by a 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol both started at the City Ground and were at fault for goal conceded in the first half before coming off at half time due to injury.

While Gvardiol has since recovered from his minor issue and represented Croatia on international duty, Guehi withdrew from the England squad with a hip problem.

However, Guehi was involved in Man City training on Thursday and is set to be available for selection against Fulham.

Clarifying Guehi’s situation following a run of error-strewn performances before his injury, Maresca said at his press conference: “He didn't join internationally because he had a small issue against Forest, but it's not because he needs some break.”

Fellow centre-back Abdukodir Khusanov pulled out of Uzbekistan duty after sustaining a knock in Man City’s defeat at Forest.

The 22-year-old was absent from all Man City photos and videos from Thursday’s training session and is now a doubt for the visit of Fulham this weekend.

Maresca has also confirmed that Matheus Nunes is a doubt with an unspecified issue; he previously missed three games in October with an ankle issue.

"From the Forest game we still have Matheus (Nunes) and [Khusanov] that are still doubts for tomorrow, because they are still with some problems. We'll see in the next hours."

The only confirmed injury absentee for Man City is attacker Antoine Semenyo, who is still recovering from a knee injury and is targeting a return next month.

Meanwhile, Maresca has confirmed one guaranteed starter for the match against Fulham, with goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma to continue between the sticks despite a poor run of form.

Donnarumma has kept just four clean sheets in 15 appearances across all competitions this season, conceding 23 goals in total, and his decision making in recent matches has come under question.

However, Maresca continues to back his fellow Italian, telling reporters: "He has been good. I think with the international team, he made a mistake in the build-up, but for Italy he was the Man of the Match in the game (vs. France), he made many good saves.

"We made some mistakes in the last games. Gigi was part of that. He is aware. Hopefully he's not going to make any more mistakes. He is going to start against Fulham."

Man City have kept just three clean sheets in their last nine meetings with Fulham, but they have won each of their last 20 head-to-head battles across all competitions – the longest winning run against the same opponent in English football history.
